# Decisions: what was decided, what was tried, and the defects that keep coming back

Patrick's rule of 14.09.2026, after a month of "one thing, then another": every decision about how the bots work is
recorded with what it answered, what it cost and how it ended, and every defect is filed under the class it belongs to.
This file is that record. Everything before 14.09.2026 was backfilled from the project's notes of 15.08–14.09.2026;
everything after is written as it happens.

Other documents answer other questions and are not repeated here: `ARCHITECTURE.md` — the shape; `MAP.md` — where a file,
a number or a log line lives; `DIALS.md` — what a number is set to; `HANDOFF.md` — the state of the work;
`RESEARCH-decisions.md` — what the literature and other games say about commitment and roles; `NIGHT-2026-09-13.md` — one
night's rounds. Where this file and the code disagree, the code is right, and this file is corrected.

**Contents** — §0 how to use this file · §1 why problems keep coming back · §2 mechanisms and their invariants · §3 defect
classes, with every recorded instance · §4 decision log · §5 structural remedies not yet built · §6 decisions waiting for
Patrick

---

## 0. How to use this file

**Before changing a mechanism**

1. Read its section in §2 and every §4 entry that names it.
2. Name the invariants the change touches. If the change removes a guard — a veto, a threshold, a window, pricing
   (`Unpaid`), learning — name what replaces it, in the same change.
3. Find the class in §3 the change is most likely to produce and read its sign.
4. Write the §4 entry with status **attempt** before deploying.

**After measuring**

- Compare sessions only at the same age from start. Turn the knob back and see the number return. Use windows longer than
  the defect takes to form — on this shard about an hour and a half for anything economic.
- Fill in *measured* and *side effects*, including a negative result, and set the status: **active**, **superseded by …**
  or **reverted**.

**When a defect is found** — add it to its class in §3. A new instance of an old class means the class is not closed by
structure; the structural remedy belongs in §5.

**Entry format (§4.1)** — *problem* (with the number that showed it) · *options* · *decision* · *expected* · *measured* ·
*side effects* · *status* · *code*.

---

## 1. Why problems keep coming back

Not because they cannot be solved. The way the work has been done guarantees that the same classes return in new places.

1. **Instances are fixed, classes are not.** Each fix closes the case in front of it — one proposer, one threshold, one
   file — and the next deed written the same way has the same defect. The failure line "the pack would not hold the Ngp
   it drew to pay with" was gated in the guild courier on 09.09, appeared again on 10.09, and on 14.09 in restocking, where
   it failed 8,719 times in half an hour.
2. **Everything is coupled.** 843 dials, 48 proposers, and flags that change how the auction treats work (`Unpaid`,
   `Steadfast`, `Summons`, `Standing`, `Committed`, `AtCounter`). A rule that is right on its own moves the equilibrium
   next to it: removing restock's refusals on the morning of 14.09 also removed the only brake on a failing trip.
3. **Verification is shorter than the defects.** Changes are measured over 15–30 minutes on a live shard; Hale's pack took
   five hours to jam, veins run out in two to three, markets warm up over an hour. There are no regression checks, so a
   fixed defect comes back somewhere else.
4. **What was learned was not read before the next change.** The lesson "unpaid work learns nothing, its proposer is its
   only gate" was written on the night of 13→14.09; restocking was made unpaid without a gate the next morning. This file
   and §0 exist for exactly that.
5. **Topics change before they close** — wars, seats, guilds, dungeons, economy, roles — and each new system leans on
   half-finished ones.

| class | instances below | last seen | closed by structure |

| C1 failure re-offered unchanged | 35 | 14.09 | no — §5 S1 |
| C2 one fact, two numbers or two questions | 37 | 14.09 night | by a rule only: derive the second from the first |
| C3 wrong shape of judgement | 18 | 14.09 | partly: veto / factor / rank / flag vocabulary |
| C4 engine rules found by symptom | 47 facts | 14.09 | no — §5 S3 for packs |
| C5 instruments that lie | 42 | 14.09 | by rules only (§2.8) |
| C6 state lost or wrongly kept across restart | 13 | 14.09 night | partly |
| C7 reach, search budget, walk orders | 21 | 14.09 | partly |

## 2. Mechanisms and their invariants

Each invariant was bought by a measured defect; the §3 references say which.

### 2.1 The auction — `BotWill`, `BotAppraisal`, `BotLedger`, `BotCommons`

One currency: takings per minute, `(Δmoney + goods made + Δskill × 500) / minutes`. A proposer offers one best deed;
`BotAppraisal.Weigh` scores it (estimate × fifth root of the factors × calling); the auction takes the best and holds it.

- **A1 — Goods bought are worth what they cost.** A purchase's `Made` is what was paid, measured around the payment; a
  guild's payment counts only the bot's own contribution. Money taken from a bot by somebody else's decision — a levy,
  a guild's draw, a counter's wages and takings, a reflex's purchase — belongs to no errand it happens to be in the
  middle of, and neither does money handed to it that way; whoever moves it books it in `BotYield.Aside` (build 45, see
  C3, 15.09). (C3: purchase as work; collective payment.)
- **A2 — Say which of four things a judgement is.** *Cannot happen* is a veto. *A poor idea* is a factor, and every factor
  that ordinary state can drive to zero has a floor. *Must come first* is a rank. *Paid nothing on purpose* is the
  `Unpaid` flag. A factor under a fifth root cannot say "cannot"; a veto cannot say "poor". (C3.)
- **A3 — A veto must not lock the work that cures its own condition.** Before adding a veto, find the remedy and check
  it is not subject to it. The overload veto of 08.09 blocked the walk to unload; the counter veto of 14.09 leaves unload
  alone, which was checked live. (C8.)
- **A4 — A deed that fails on its first beat is not offered unchanged at the next review.** Either the proposer asks the
  question the deed fails on, or the failure is learned. Unpaid work learns nothing, so an `Unpaid` flag arrives with a
  gate for every reason the deed can fail. (C1.)
- **A5 — A check belongs in the choice, not in the work.** Skipping a candidate is free; failing a deed is a loop. (C1.)
- **A6 — A proposer refuses everything its deed will refuse**, asking the same question with the same numbers. (C1, C2.)
- **A7 — Anything created in `Propose` is created for an offer.** The auction calls `Drop` only on the winner; losers are
  discarded. Claims made at offer time are short (`BotOffice.Offering`, 12 s); companies form on the winner's first
  `Advance`. (C9.)
- **A8 — A road that does not exist is not a price.** Unreached work writes nothing into land, commons or trade
  (`Settle(unreached)`); the road note (`Beware`) is still written. (C3.)
- **A9 — An estimate that can only be corrected by winning does not open below the winners.** (C3: forge 55.)
- **A10 — A lesson is filed under the name the chooser reads it by** (trade vs place). (C1, C10.)
- **A11 — Commitment is by events, not bonuses.** Steadfast work is held for its reckoning; only what will not wait
  (`Pressing`), a call from outside (`Summons`) or trouble in the work gets through; displaced work is put down and taken
  up again. A bonus only moves the point at which two choices trade places. (C11.)
- **A12 — What an appraisal cannot see is not undone by a rank or a veto.** Work that has already spent money in its
  middle is `Committed`. (C3: rank outranked a purchase.)

### 2.2 Deeds and proposers — the contract

- **D1 — The deed owns its whole chain, and no state waits indefinitely.** Every "stand and wait" ends on the beat it
  stops being true. (C1: frozen work.)
- **D2 — Every new gate gets a named counter in the same change**, incremented where the event happens, not behind
  another gate, and the gates add up to the proposer's `Asked`. (C5.)
- **D3 — A repeated walk order is bitwise identical.** (C7.)
- **D4 — Engine results that arrive on a timer are read on the next beat** (crafting, harvesting); an exit on "the
  material is gone" waits one swing. (C4.)
- **D5 — A deed that stands still on purpose says so** (`BotDeed.Still`), and skips are counted. (C5: progress read from a
  display string.)
- **D6 — Whatever is placed at an offset from a settled point asks about the tiles it lands on.** (C7: camps in water.)

### 2.3 Walking and reach — `BotWalk`, `BotPath`, `BotReach`, `BotRefused`, `BotBarred`, `BotQuad`

- **W1 — "Cannot get there" is proven from the far side** (a flood from the target, `BotPath.Enclose`), never from the
  bot's side, at any budget. (C7.)
- **W2 — Errands keep the full search ceiling; it is what finds a shop's door.** Walks re-issued every beat (formation
  stations, sweeps) get a short look (`StationCeilingMs` 15). (C7.)
- **W3 — Only `Refused` and `GaveUp` are proven refusals of a road.** `Stalled` in a crowd is not. (C7.)
- **W4 — Distance is a price, not a wall.** A general limit applies where the whole population pays, not to rare work.
  (C7.)
- **W5 — Height comes from the source the consumer compares with:** walking `BotStep.Settle`, building `GetAverageZ`.
  (C7.)
- **W6 — A measurement rests and clears on arrival; an assertion does not.** Decided walls are `BotBarred`, never
  `BotRefused`. (C10.)
- **W7 — Area sampling uses positive knowledge** (`BotQuad.Trodden`), not negative notes. (C7.)
- **W8 — Pursuit is excluded from "stopped closing", and a chase has a leash from where it began.** (C7.)

### 2.4 Market and money — `BotAuction`, `BotShops`, `BotUnload`, `BotShelf`, `BotYield`

- **M1 — Coin stays in the world when bots trade.** Ties between a stall and a counter go to the stall; a bot never opens
  above what a shopkeeper asks (`BotShops.Shelf`). (C2.)
- **M2 — Supply and demand must cross** (`BotAuction.Cross`); a material is ordered only if some bot's work produces it; a
  maker reads paid wants first. (C12.)
- **M3 — Only a user of a material keeps a stock of it; keep lists are quantities, never `int.MaxValue`.** (C2.)
- **M4 — Every surplus has a door:** the market, the bank box, and the ground as a last resort. Nothing is put into a pack
  past the engine's cap without asking (`TryDropItem`); anything that changes money over a counter first asks whether the
  pack can take a coin (`BotYield.Pocket`). (C4, C8.)
- **M5 — Money is where the engine spends it.** A bill under 2,000gp is paid from the backpack; purchases draw the
  shortfall from the bank into the pack first. (C4.)

### 2.5 Companies, guilds and wars — `BotSquad`, `BotGuilds`, `BotEstate`, `BotWar`, `BotFeud`

- **G1 — A Bound bot has no auction, so whoever binds it gives it work or releases it.** A company's charge is held by an
  errand; whoever charged a company ends it; a dissolved company is flagged so nobody joins it. (C8, C10.)
- **G2 — A consequence at the end of a process requires that the process can end.** Opinions are settled at a war's end;
  kills inside a war do not move opinion. (C8.)
- **G3 — One appointed hand is a veto.** Offer to every member and remove the race with a claim the work renews. (C3.)
- **G4 — A rule about a group is applied to the group** (guild muster once, after the population exists). (C3.)
- **G5 — Wars, truces, clocks, move debts and opinions survive a restart**; the engine's enemy lists are re-asserted at
  start. A restart is safe except in the middle of a hall move. (C6.)

### 2.6 Minds — `BotMindAI`

- **N1 — A mind chooses from an enumeration; its choice becomes a real deed in the same auction; its forecast is
  measured, never bid** (bid = the deed's own worth × `Insistence`). (C3.)
- **N2 — Narrow the enumeration instead of persuading; `none` first; names only from living lists.** (C3, C5.)
- **N3 — Minds are shown what the others hold, and asked at staggered times.** (C11.)
- **N4 — Prompt wording is a defect surface:** a count whose good value is zero reads as good, a word carries its scale,
  one phrase per reason. (C5.)

### 2.7 Observation — summaries, alarms, dials, Argus

- **O1 — Engine measurements are facts; a model's findings are conjectures.** `props`, `tile`, `near`, `pack`, `sight`,
  `road` are trusted; watcher findings are checked against the log before anything is changed. (C5.)
- **O2 — Summary counters are cumulative since the world loaded.** Rates are differences; sessions compare only at equal
  age; every knob is turned back before its effect is believed. (C5.)
- **O3 — Throttle lines, never counters.** Every number has a denominator taken from successes; a counter behind a gate
  measures the gate; a number nobody prints is worse than none; a ceiling that is reached says so. (C5.)
- **O4 — Verification order: the config file, then the boot line, then the code.** A background check fixes its log file
  name at launch; the clock is checked before conclusions about a log's age. (C5.)
- **O5 — An alarm carries numerator, denominator and measured window.** A population alarm can be tripped by one looping
  bot, so the first action on any alarm is to group the window's failures by bot and reason. (C5.)
- **O6 — Build with the shard stopped when `mindedBots` changed** (a running shard hides BotMindAI's errors); `do save`
  before stopping (a kill rolls the world back to the last autosave). (C5, C6.)

### 2.8 What survives a restart

| survives | lost |
|---|---|
| the world save (`Saves/Mobiles`, `Saves/Items` — Patrick's character lives there; **never delete**) | ~~the bots themselves~~ — since build 163 bots come back with place, pack, bank, skills, ledger **and guild** (build 170); a bot dead at the save is raised by the reviver (build 172) |
| skills, fame, karma (`Saves/BotProgress`) | purses and packs (`BotProgress.Savings` off by Patrick's order, 08.09) |
| island map, pins, trodden ground (`Saves/BotQuads`) | ledgers and commons (what work paid where) |
| guild claims (`Saves/BotClaims`), hand-set seats (`Saves/BotSeats`) | the market (stalls and wants) |
| wars, truces, clocks, move debts, opinions (`Saves/BotWars`) | reach pockets (`BotReach`) |
| guild halls and merchants' shelves (in the world) | veins, counters, hearths (`BotGround`) |
| dungeon halls (`bot-dungeon-halls.json`), minds' lessons (`bot-minds.json`) | dials changed through the door |

## 3. Defect classes, with every recorded instance

Dates are 2026; "v1" is the first bot assembly, deleted on 21.08. Numbers are as measured at the time.

### C1 — A failure re-offered unchanged

**Definition.** A deed fails, and the same deed is offered to the same bot at the next review, because nothing between
the failure and the choice remembers it: the proposer does not ask the failing question, the note is written where no
chooser reads it, or the work is unpaid and learns nothing.
**Sign.** One bot, one reason, hundreds of `failed at <kind>` in minutes; a population alarm with one name under it.
**Structural remedy.** None built. §5 S1.

### C2 — One fact, two numbers or two questions

**Definition.** Two numbers, or two calls, describe one thing, live in different places and agree by coincidence — until
one moves and the system parks in the band between them.
**Sign.** "Nothing happens", with no error; two numbers in one summary line that never meet; a proposer and its deed
disagreeing. **Remedy (rule).** Derive the second number from the first; ask one method from every place.

### C3 — The wrong shape of judgement

**Definition.** A true statement about work expressed in the wrong form: a veto where a factor belongs or the reverse, a
price on work that earns nothing by design, one number serving as both forecast and bid.
**Sign.** Refusals naming the same reason across bots ("expected to pay −N"); work taken but never won; a whole trade
disappearing from the island. **Remedy (partial).** The vocabulary in §2.1 A2.

## 4. Decision log

### 4.1 Full entries, newest first

**01.10.2026 · build 380 (written by Opus, night) · A bot levied for a harrowing falls in**
- *Patrick, 01.10 ~23:15:* «why the hell did Cedric gather a group of 6, and all these 6 idiots stand in the town and do not move?»
- *Measured on 379:* Cedric the Captain took the first harrowing of the boot at 23:10:40 — (765, 1035), where 4 had died — and his muster at (1284, 1534) read "1 of 6 standing in it, 6 in the company" from 23:12:38 for five minutes; the five members stood in Britain: Gunnloda foraging, Brynhild brewing, Bardryn carrying a pack to the bank, Maud and Oriel holding nothing.
- *Why:* `BotHarrow.Take` joined each bot to the company (`BotSquads.Join`) and left its work in its hands — the fault build 299 closed for delves (`BotDelve.Levy` presses a `BotEnlist`) and `BotSweep` closed for sweeps, never for the harrowing. The same holds for `BotBand`, `BotProwl`'s raised company and `BotScout` (passed to the groups agent, who owns them tonight).
- *Decision (`BotHarrow.Take`, `Pressed`):* after joining, the enlistment is pressed on the bot (`BotWill.Press(other, new BotEnlist(squad, _map, _muster, true), …)`): its errand is put down and it walks to the muster.
- *Watch:* "pressed to fall in" in the harrow's line; musters reaching their company.

**01.10.2026 · build 379 (written by Opus, night) · A guild's buildings stand on the mainland; a wipe keeps the roads and the danger map**
- *Patrick, 30.09 ~23:00 (the night's order, `scratchpad/agents/night-0930-order.md`):* a wipe after the key changes — «we raze the guild buildings and halls and zero the bots' knowledge), paths and what is known of the zones live on, and the bots can still improve them»; key change 1: «Guilds may buy and place halls only on the main island of Britannia». His answers: the wipe is everything from zero (skills, progress, gold, items, memory); the changes come first, the wipe after.
- *Measured on 375–378 (22:52 log at 14 minutes):* the zones' hunting ground was named 2467 times and chosen 343, but prowls ending "nothing here" rose to 61 of 158 (39 %, ~30 % before): by the zone level at the prowl's point, hostile zones 20 empty of 33, clear zones 27 of 71, no zone 14 of 50 — the prowl is sent to a spawner's tile and searches 30 tiles round it while the creatures patrol up to 64 (handed to the groups agent, who owns the hunt tonight). Delves: 3 calls left to one already gathering near them (376/378), no second call beside a first.
- *Decision, the mainland (`BotPlot.Mainland`, `FindHome`; `Ashore`, `OffMainland`, `GatesUnread`; `BotGuildHouses.Fit`):* every guild building `BotPlot.Find` places — the first hall, a bigger one, an outpost, a hall carried away — lies on the land of the population's home (`BotGates.LandOf`); a search begun from a seat on an island begins at the home; nothing is placed before the gates are read. A guild's house in a town is taken only in a mainland town. A bot's own house keeps any land (`BotAbode` → `FindHome`).
- *Decision, the wipe (`BotHand.ResetPopulation`):* `BotQuad.Forget` and `BotRoadbook.Forget` are no longer called — the blood by square and the roads walked live on with the zones' file and the navigation graph; everything else the reset wiped it still wipes.
- *Watch:* the plots' line ("guild buildings kept to the mainland"); after the wipe, where the first halls go up.

**30.09.2026 · build 378 (written by Opus, night) · A delve offered holds its ground before its call is under way**
- *Measured on 377 at a minute:* companies run again — Dalla's four made 15 tiles in 4 s (about 3.7 a second, against 1.2 on 376). But right after the restart two calls began two tiles apart: Mirthal at (1109, 1917) and Brom at (1110, 1915), both of Faunalyn's old company, offered in the same beat.
- *Why:* 376's list of calls (`BotDelve._callsNow`) is filled on a call's first beat, and every leader asked in the same beat was offered its own before any call was on the list.
- *Decision (`BotDelve.Offering`, `_offersNow`, `OfferHoldMs` 15 s):* the proposer notes each delve it offers, with the leader and its place; `CallingNear` reads these offers as well as the calls under way, so a second leader within reach in the same beat is left to the first.
- *Watch:* "left to a call already gathering near them"; no two "is calling a party" lines within `BotDelve.Reach` of each other in the same minute.

**30.09.2026 · build 377 (written by Opus, night) · Companies run again: behind is past the close-up and a margin, and a slowed leader walks**
- *Patrick, 30.09 ~22:45:* «watch Faunalyn — why does she step one tile at a time in the group…», then «look how the groups move: they used to run, and now they step one tile a tick — that is clearly a problem».
- *Measured on 376:* Faunalyn's party (the first to go down after 376 — one call, seven of several guilds) marched from Britain at about 1.2 tiles a second (1249,1624 → 1223,1677 in 42 s) with every member within eight tiles of her; "turns a marching leader was slowed to for a member behind it" 352 in eight minutes (2012 on 371, 2402 on 363). The route itself is long by the ground, not by the zones: Argus's `nav 1385 1635 1013 1434` drew 118 points at 8741 steps of cost with the zones priced and 117 at 6857 without, both first heading south round the mountains.
- *Why:* build 340's `BotSquad.Lagging` counted a member behind at more than `BotEnlist.CloseUp` (6) — the very distance at which a member closing up stops and then keeps the leader's pace — so the tail of any column was behind on almost every turn and the leader went at half a walk (twice its walking step, 800ms a tile) for the whole road. Two thresholds on one shelf.
- *Decision (`BotSquad.LagBeyond` 6, `PacedSteps` 1):* a member is behind only past CloseUp + 6 (twelve tiles), and a slowed leader goes at its walk, not half of it, while its members run to close.
- *Watch:* "turns a marching leader was slowed" (should fall to a fraction); a march's tiles a second; members left behind on the march (`LeftBehind`).

**30.09.2026 · build 376 (written by Opus, night) · One delve call at a time round a muster**
- *Measured with 371's instrument (the "passed over within reach" clause), 19:58–22:34:* Faunalyn "only 3 of the 12 … of 3 called … passed over within reach: 17 in a company already, 2 producers, 4 without supplies", Yngrid the same second "only 5 … 17 in a company already", Brokk "only 2 … 16 in a company already, 1 unable to fight, 5 producers, 5 without supplies". The largest filter by far is "in a company already".
- *Why:* since build 370 a call takes any guild's bots but a hostile one's, and the calls of different guilds ran side by side over the same bots — Faunalyn and Yngrid at (1167, 1856) at 19:59–20:00; Miriel at (1169, 1851), Faunalyn at (1168, 1856) and Brokk at (1254, 1803) all at 20:05:07; Faunalyn and Brokk 25 tiles apart at 22:31:01 — each call's company holding what the next one needed, and every one of them failing. The guild spacing (`BotDelver.BetweenMs`) only ever kept a guild from calling twice.
- *Decision (`BotDelve._callsNow`, `CallingNear`; `BotDelver.Answering`):* the calls gathering now are kept in one list (dropped when the call marches, ends or its leader dies, or after twice `MusterMs`); a leader within `BotDelve.Reach` of a call whose leader is not hostile to it is not offered a delve of its own, and is levied into that call like any bot.
- *Watch:* "left to a call already gathering near them" in `Delving:`; the "in a company already" part of failed calls; whether a call reaches its floor.

**30.09.2026 · build 375 (written by Opus, night) · The hunt reads the zones**
- *Patrick, 30.09 ~18:35, point 3 of the zones order:* the zones' precision "directly drives the safe paths and the quality of the bots' hunting". Paths read them since 373.
- *Measured before it:* prowls ending "nothing here" — 67 of 217 taken on 371 (31 %), 35 of 120 on 373 (29 %); deaths on prowl or hunt 2 on 371 (60 minutes) and 5 on 373 (16 minutes). The shard was paused 20:11–22:30 at Patrick's word and started again on 374; the zones came back from their file ("233 haunts matched, 2166 observed cells, saved 152 minutes ago").
- *Why:* the hunter's ground is eight random darts round home plus four named grounds (where blood is spilt, where hunting paid, where the quadrant record says it hurt, where the guild's material walks) and the quadrant's strength gate; none of them says where the quarry lives now or how many of it will come at once, and a third of the prowls find nothing.
- *Decision (`BotHunter.ReadsZones`, `Zoned`, `ZoneDare` 1.0; counters `ZoneOffered`, `ZoneChosen`, `ZoneDeadly`, `ZoneTooStrong`):* a fifth named ground — the land zone within the roam with living quarry whose fight (`BotZone.Threat`: the strongest in full and the rest that can close at once) is at most the hunter's strength (a company's when it has one), scored by quarry × (½ + threat/strength) over distance, passive-only grounds at half their number, deadly zones never; its `Stand` tile is the candidate. And every candidate is weighed by its zone: a deadly zone makes it lethal, a hostile one whose threat outweighs the hunter makes it ground the hunter does not dare alone — both then go the company's way or are passed over, as any ground too strong.
- *Watch:* the zones' clause in the hunter's line (named / chosen / made lethal / too strong); prowls ending "nothing here" (from ~30 %); deaths on prowl and hunt; hunt's finished share.

**30.09.2026 · build 374 (written by Opus, evening) · A march's clock stands still while the company fights**
- *Patrick, 30.09 ~20:05:* «when they fight on the way to the goal, their timer stands still, because they are fighting».
- *Measured on 373 at 10 minutes:* paths fixed 99.3 %, chase 98.1 %, station 98.8 %; searches 0.59ms each (371 at the same age 0.36ms, 370 0.86ms); the zones priced 1.09M nodes in a fringe, 0.81M hostile and 0.42M deadly of 14.2M asked in the first five minutes; the population's tick 4.23ms a look; work 94.7 % on the page.
- *Why:* fights on the road already stopped the march's fifteen minutes (`BotDelve.MarchMs`), but only up to `MarchFightMs` (five minutes) in all — Daeron's nine on 371 halted four times on 240 tiles and were given up at fifteen. Ordinary work already works so: a piece of work put down for a fight moves its stake's clock by the time it was away (`BotWill.Moved`), so only the march had a cap.
- *Decision (`BotDelve.MarchFightMs` 300000 → 0 = no limit):* every fight the company stands to on the march (and on the way back to the muster) is off the march's clock.
- *Watch:* "never reached the mouth in 15 minutes" in `Delving:`; a march's whole length when a party goes down.

**30.09.2026 · build 373 (written by Opus, evening) · The roads read the zones**
- *Measured on 372 at 5 minutes:* 818 zones (123 clear, 388 hostile, 307 deadly, 256 of them at sea) off 1651 spawners and 12760 creatures; the median bot 1477. The zones' beat cost 0.466ms a 250ms beat (0.2 % of the loop), builds 93ms average off the loop, the JSON 1.4 MB. Deaths since the start by where they fell: 6 deadly, 9 hostile, 0 in a fringe, 0 on clear ground. The tour: four debuggers (Argus, Lynceus, Heimdall, Hermes) holding 75 s at a zone each, 12 of 439 land zones stood in the first five minutes. On the page the zones draw round Britain as separate shapes ("trolls and ettins, S of Britain", "gargoyles and reapers, N of Britain").
- *Why:* Patrick's third point — where no creature patrols the bots route through confidently; where a patrol or its aggro reach could touch them, the ground is potentially dangerous — and Daeron's party on 371 halted four times on 240 tiles from Britain to the Orc Caves' mouth to turn on attackers. The planners already ask `NavigationService.Danger` per node (`BotDanger.Cost`: blood +60, bars +800).
- *Decision (`BotDanger.ZonesPriced`, `EdgePerBot` 10 up to `EdgeMost` 40, `HostilePerBot` 30 between `HostileLeast` 20 and `HostileMost` 150, `DeadlyCost` 300; counters `InFringe`, `InHostile`, `InDeadly`):* a node's extra cost is the larger of the blood and the zone's price by `BotZones.LevelAt` (×vsBot of the zone); clear ground and hunting grounds cost nothing; bars keep their 800. Bounded so the planners' int costs cannot overflow.
- *Watch:* the zones' clause in `Getting about:` (the danger part); deaths by where they fell in `Zones:` (fringe and clear should stay near nought); paths reached (the detours must not cost the 99 %); route lengths and the slow ticks (a detour is a longer search).

**30.09.2026 · build 372 (written by an Opus agent, evening) · Danger and safety zones: what attacks where, how far it sees, how strong it is, and a tour that wakes the ground to learn it**
- *Patrick's order of 30.09.2026, ~18:35:* walk the world with Argus and the other debuggers, mark every mob zone with how many live there and how strong they are; put the zones on the dashboard as separate areas that live in memory, update, have smoothed corners and grow more precise; where no mobs are, bots route safe paths through; where a patrol or its aggro could touch someone, the ground is potentially dangerous — "maximum precision: it drives safe paths and the quality of the hunting".
- *Why a new mechanism rather than more of the old ones:* the danger the shard knew was learned from blood (`BotQuad.Muscle`, `BotPeril`, `BotBarred`) — a square is dangerous after bots have died in it. Nothing knew where creatures that attack on sight actually are before the first death. And nothing could learn it by watching: the world sleeps wherever no client is (`BotWake`), so a creature nobody is near stands at its spawn point and its patrol is invisible. From the analysts (`zones-data/`, 3474 bot deaths on 29–30.09): 54 % of deaths are lone bots, 10.3 % fell in squares the shard's own threat scan read as zero, and 78 were companies of 3–6 strong bots killed by one weak kind (snakes, zombies, skeletons) — the worst creature nearby was weak and there were many of it. The sea spawners declare walking ranges of 100–175 tiles, and a naive union of declared discs fuses them into ocean-basin mega-zones.
- *Decision — the model (`BotZones`, `BotHaunts`/`BotHaunt`/`BotZoneKind`, `BotZoneScan`, `BotZoneRaster`, `BotZoneBuild`):* every spawner of the home map is a haunt, read in strips a beat (`map.GetItemsInBounds<BaseSpawner>`, 28 strips, again every 30 min). A kind's traits (attacks first = `Closest`/`Strongest`/`Weakest`; caster = `AI_Mage`; `RangePerception`; sea = `CantWalk && CanSwim`; rooted = `CantWalk && !CanSwim`; townsfolk = vendor, escort, invulnerable) are read off a living one, or off the one specimen `BotDungeon.Might` already builds (new `BotDungeon.Traits`, same construction, never twice). The sweep passes every creature every ~15 s, a window of 8×8 sectors at a time within 0.6 ms a beat, and records each attacker seen *awake* (`AITimer.Running`) into a raster of 4-tile cells fading with a 6 h half-life; a sleeping creature's position is kept as presence, never as patrol. Each haunt learns its awake seconds, sightings and the farthest a creature was seen from home (`patrol.observed`).
- *Decision — the zones:* three layers, never merged across. **Land attackers:** declared disc of the walking range (up to `DeclaredMost` 64 tiles; wider spawners paint only their living, 12 tiles round each), every living attacker (4 tiles), every observed cell (±1 cell). **Sea:** creatures that cannot leave water — and amphibious ones standing on water — paint only 8 tiles round themselves, grouped into one zone within 40; they reach 3 tiles ashore by bite, 12 by spell; never toured. **Hunting grounds:** passive animals, only where no attacker patrols. A zone is a connected patch of one layer (8-way). Its aggro fringe is the patch dilated by the reach of what patrols it (chamfer distance, sight capped at 20). Threat is what can converge: round every living attacker, all others within 20 tiles, the strongest in full and the rest at `BotThreat.Secondary`; the zone's threat is the worst such crowd, `vsBot` = threat ÷ the median living bot's `BotThreat.Power` (every 2 min). Levels: `hostile`; `deadly` at ×6 or after 6 bot deaths in it in 24 h; `clear` for hunting grounds. **`edge` is a cell's answer, never a zone's own level** — the fringe band is the edge; `counts.edge` stays 0. A haunt whose creatures are all dead is still `hostile`, at half its declared fight (`EmptyWeight`), because its spawner fills it within minutes. Once a haunt's confidence (half awake seconds against 600, half sightings against 60) reaches 0.8, its disc shrinks to its observed reach plus a cell and the observed cells draw the rest. Zone numbers are kept across builds by overlap with each old zone's own cells, family by family.
- *Decision — cost and threads:* the queries are one read of the published raster: `BotZones.LevelAt(map, x, y)` and `LevelAt(map, x, y, out vsBot, out threat)` (~5–10 ns), `BotZones.ZoneAt(map, x, y)`, `BotZones.Find(id)`. The loop does the survey strip, the sweep (budgeted and measured), the tour (1 s), and every 20 s a gather of plain values; the build — painting, labelling, fringes, marching squares (d3's case table), Douglas–Peucker, Chaikin ×2 and the zones' JSON — is pure arithmetic on that copy and runs off the loop on ≥ 4 cores (this machine has 16), published through the one volatile `BotZones.State` (CLAUDE.md rules 3, 10); a build gathered before a world reload is recognised by its generation and dropped. Outlines are cached by shape, so a zone whose cells did not change is not traced again. Measured on the spawn files with every spawner full (14 647 creatures): first build 373 ms, a rebuild with nothing moved 102 ms, with everyone moved 8 tiles 277 ms (764 of 859 zones kept their number); 843 zones, 1.47 MB of JSON. With fewer cores the build runs on the loop at most every 2 min (`InlineRefreshMs`).
- *Decision — the tour (`BotZoneTour`, hooks filled by `BotDebugModule`):* the free debuggers (`BotVigil.Walkers`: a body, not witnessing, not charting) each take the zone with the fewest awake seconds (60 s buckets, nearest within a bucket), are carried there by their own teleport (`BotVigil.Carry` → `BotDebugger.Hover`), wake the client's 5×5 sectors round the stand and the zone's box up to 81 sectors, pass the woken box every 2 s, hold 75 s, and go on; a round ends when every land zone has been stood in once. It never undoes the bots' waking: a sector goes back to sleep only if the tour woke it, no bot needs it (`BotWake.Needed`) and no client is near; `BotWake` hands a sector the tour holds over to it (`BotZoneTour.Adopt`) instead of putting it to sleep. The vigil does not move a walker off a stop (`BotZoneTour.Holding`).
- *Decision — memory, deaths, door, web:* what was learned (haunts' awake seconds, sightings, reach, tour stops; observed cells) is kept in `Data/bot-zones-seen.json`, read and written off the loop every 10 min — not a save store, because a store that cannot read its shape stops the shard on a prompt; an unreadable file is logged and ignored. `BotMobile.OnDeath` → `BotZones.Fell` counts each death where it fell. Door: `do zones`, `do zones tour on|off`, `do zone x y` (by hand only). `/api/zones` in `BotWebServer`, with an `ETag` and `304`. Config `Configuration/bot-zones.json`, every threshold a dial. One `Zones:` line every 5 minutes.
- *Validation (offline, the real builder on `Data/Spawns/shared/felucca` with every spawner full at random places in its spawn square, no observation, deaths not promoting, median bot 2000):* of 3433 outdoor deaths of 29–30.09, 45.0 % fell inside a hostile patrol and 2.0 % inside a deadly one, 21.8 % in an aggro fringe, 31.2 % on clear ground (23.1 % nobody's, 8.0 % inside a hunting ground) — and those were killed almost all by attackers standing outside their declared ground (giant spiders, gargoyles, trolls, gazers, plague spawn): wandering and chasing, which only the awake observation and the living positions can draw. Island block covered: 7.0 % hostile, 1.3 % deadly, 15.5 % fringe. The zones with the most deaths read ×1.0–2.1 with 5–11 attackers converging — the analysts' swarm, not a single strong creature — which is why deaths promote.
- *Watch:* the `Zones:` line — zones by level, empty hostile ones, deaths by where they fell (the share on clear ground should fall as observation grows), the sweep's ms a window and awake share, observed cells, the tour's round and stops, `gather`, build phases and ms off the loop, JSON KB. The first build's line at boot. `LeftToTour` in the `Wake:` line.

- *Deployed as observation only (Opus, 19:45):* nothing reads the zones yet — routing (`BotDanger.Cost`) and hunting are wired in the next build, once the live `Zones:` line and the page show the map is sound. Measured on 371 at 20 minutes before it: honest 92 %; the capital took 60 % of the gold sold over shopkeepers' counters (the day's 43 %), 126gp of premium over 8 sales; Daeron's party went down 9 strong from Britain with bots of several guilds (the first party of the day since 360) and did not reach the Orc Caves' mouth at (1013, 1434) in 15 minutes, halting four times to turn on attackers.

**30.09.2026 · build 371 (written by an Opus agent, evening) · Britain the centre of trade: the capital's counters pay a quarter more out of the city's purse, a stall's load walks to them when that pays for the road, a trader's journey goes there**
- *Patrick, 30.09 evening:* «rework the trade: the traders must put Britain first as the centre of trade» (the morning's «shops may be placed, preferably in Britain» is builds 355/358: `BotShopkeeper.Britain`, `BritainReach` 200).
- *The trade map, as the code chose places before this build:* selling to a shopkeeper (`BotPeddler` → `BotShops.Buyer`: the nearest buyer by distance alone, no sealed or unplaced test; `FromThePack` the same); buying from one (`BotShopper`: a bot's shop if it `Beats` the rest on price and a walk priced at `WalkGold`, then the placeless stall, then the guild's counter, then `BotShops.Nearest` — the nearest, cautious/sealed/unplaced passed over; every craft's input — sew, brew, fletch, inscribe, acquire, runes, contracts, kindling, boats — through the same `Nearest`); the porter (`BotGround.Counter`: the nearest bank, two passes; the market it lists on is placeless and the bank box global); the bots' shops (Britain's bank within 200, else the bank by home within 240; customers within `SeekTiles` 240); the guild's courier (`BotSupplier`: `Nearest` from the courier, for the only hall, The Crown's at Skara Brae); `BotBurgh` (a guild's standing in a town moves what it pays at the counter, ±10 %, after the place is chosen, never the choice); the market (`BotAuction`, `BotCity`: no place at all); `BotTraveller` (a random reachable town, curiosity-weighted).
- *Measured on the day's events (`logs/bot-events.ndjson`, 00:00–18:40, each ending placed at the nearest town within 250 tiles):* purchases from shopkeepers 3865 for 120124gp — Britain 2031 (52.5 %, 64524gp), Vesper 581, Skara Brae 478, Jhelom 356, Minoc 268, Cove 79, Yew 41; sales to them 1268 for 83463gp — Britain 560 (44 %, 36091gp), Vesper 196, Minoc 163 (16968gp, ingots), Skara Brae 161 (19827gp), Jhelom 103, Yew 53; unloads that left something 1158 — Britain 510, Vesper 208, Skara Brae 203, Minoc 163; bots' shop shifts 341 — Britain 108 (27 sold anything, 815gp), Jhelom 80 (9, 246gp), Skara Brae 75 (14, 361gp), Minoc 43 (4, 90gp), Yew 22 (1, 60gp), Vesper 13 (0); guild counter 56 supplies, all Skara Brae; stall purchases 3169 (67590gp), placeless. The live session (17:58–18:40) the same shape: Britain 40 % of counter purchases, 39 % of sales, 16 % of unloads, 19 % of shifts.
- *Why:* Britain carries half the counter trade only because half the counters and a quarter of the bots are there: every chooser is "the nearest", and every other town stands 800–2200 tiles off (Skara Brae 803, Cove 826, Yew 992, Trinsic 1124, Minoc 1129, Vesper 1478, Jhelom 2200). Of the 3865 purchases only 21 began within 600 tiles of Britain and were made elsewhere; of 1268 sales, 4. Nothing made the capital worth a road — and a road is not free: after build 350 restocks that walked 600 tiles or more died 22 times in 191 (11.5 %) against 0.8 % under 200, peddles over 500 tiles 28 of 57 before build 350's petty gate (1 of 14 since), journeys between towns 51 of 195. So the capital is made a price, not a rule, and consumers keep buying at the nearest counter: at a tenth off, 20 of the day's restocks would have moved.
- *Decision, the capital's price (`BotCapital`: `Premium` 1.25, `Factor`, `Reserve` → `BotCity.FairReserve` 2000; `BotCity.Draw`, `Holds`, `CapitalPaid`; `BotShops.Sell(…, out premium)`):* a sale over a counter in Britain's box (`BotTowns.Of`) is paid a quarter more by the city, out of the treasury above the fair's reserve — a lever with a budget, never more than the mint (3000/h), stopped by an empty purse like a buy or a fair — into the pack, the account, or the pack regardless. Never above the island's lowest ask for the thing (`BotShops.Lowest`): a counter paying more than a shelf asks is a carousel (v1's four thousand ginseng sales), so iron ingots (4 against 5) and bloodmoss keep the whole quarter, leather a fifth, arrows nothing, goods no shopkeeper sells the whole quarter, goods of quality already at the shelf's price nothing. The "sold N things to X for Ngp" line keeps the shopkeeper's gold only (watch-shard.sh reads it); the premium has its own line, "was paid Ngp more by the city for selling … at the capital's counter".
- *Decision, the sale's counter (`BotShops.Buyer(bot, item, units, stall, out price, out factor, out nearer)`, `BotCapital.Pull`, `BotPeddle` `factor`/`passed`):* every buyer is weighed at units × its price × the premium − tiles × `BotPeddler.PettyPerTile` (0.1, the number the "worth less than the walk" gate reads — the chooser and the gate cannot disagree); the premium counts only for a load on a stall (it rides safe in the market until the counter), a counter within the bot's own leash from home (`BotPopulation.Leash`: newcomers trade at home), within `Reach` (1000) of the bot, on a land the gates join, with the treasury above its reserve. Pack goods go to the best buyer at its own price (a death would lose them). Among buyers paying the same the nearest wins, as before. The buyer's side now also passes over counters the graph places no tile beside or the shard has proved sealed (`Unplaced`, `BotReach`), as `Nearest` has since build 357. A peddle's claim and its petty gate carry the premium the chooser counted. By the day's events up to some twenty loads a day (≈12000gp, mostly ingots from Skara Brae, Cove and Yew) would have walked to Britain — fewer once the leash and the shelf's cap are counted; at ×1.5 about twice as many.
- *Decision, the trader's journey (`BotTraveller`, `BotCapital.Trader`, `Journeys`, `Unroaded`, `KeptAtCapital`):* a bot holding a shop's worth of what the island asks for (`BotShopkeep.Look` against `OpenWorth`, the very test that offers a shift; not red, criminal or of The Shadow), offered a journey behind the same gates as any (progress, two hours, fit, supplied, a road within its strength and `Furthest`), goes to the capital; standing in it (the nearest town), it is not offered a journey away. It arrives within `ShiftReach` of Britain's bank, so its next shift is offered there. `BotShopkeeper.Britain` reads the town from `BotCapital.Name`.
- *Not changed, and why:* buying (consumers keep the nearest counter — no price difference between towns pays 800 tiles of road at 11.5 % deaths); the porter (the bank box is global and the market placeless: the bank chosen changes only the walk); the guild's courier (one hall, at Skara Brae); `BotBurgh`; the bots' shops' reaches (358's measured 200s).
- *Config (`bot-shops.json`, PascalCase):* `CapitalRunning`, `Capital`, `CapitalPremium`, `CapitalReach`. Dials: `BotCapital.Running`, `Name`, `Premium`, `Reach`, `Reserve`. Off: `dial BotCapital.Running false` — every counter chosen at its own price, nothing paid on top, travellers as before.
- *Watch:* `Trade:` — "the capital (Britain) — N sales over its counters … (P % of the gold)" (the day's share 43 %), "Xgp paid on top by the city at ×1.25 over N sales, S short" (expected 300–450gp an hour; short only during a fair), "N peddles offered past a nearer buyer and M sold there (… tiles further)" (about one an hour), "its price not counted … beyond the bot's leash, … beyond 1000 tiles, … on a land no gate joins, … with the treasury at its reserve and … for goods carried in the pack", purchases and shop shifts at the capital against elsewhere; `City:` "Ngp paid on top of the capital's counters" against the treasury and the fairs; `Travel:` "K traders kept in the capital and J sent to it"; `Bot shops:` "sent to Britain's bank"; deaths doing peddle and the breaker's peddle rests (a pulled load that dies on the road is the risk — the levers are `CapitalReach`, `PettyPerTile`, `CapitalPremium`); "counters passed over for having no way through" rises by construction (the seller's chooser now asks it too).
- *Also:* `MAP.md` and `DIALS.md` want `python regen-map.py` (new file `BotShops/BotCapital.cs`, five dials, the `Trade:` line's new clause, the city's new clause, the traveller's); `BotShops/README.md` has a section "The capital".

- *Decision 4, the gate past the easiest (`BotDelver.Ringed`, `Enough`, `Cored`, `Fits`, `RingCompany`, counter `Uncompanied`):* with `BotProving.Judges` and `RoomGate`, a dungeon past the easiest is judged by the room its guild's company cleared lately, not by ×`Odds` the worst creature: the leader and every guildmate counted still worth a fifth of the worst (`WeakestShare`), and as many of the guild's own fighters — the leader counted if it fights — as the ring fields for it now (`RingCompany`: the party's size, or every fighter the guild has if fewer), in reach at the offer and standing at the muster at the descent (`Recheck`, which now says why a party is sent elsewhere). - *Decision 5, the leader's target (`BotSquads.Note`, `Guards`, `LeaderReach` 2, counter `LeaderGuarded`):* verified in code — the company's enemy is the leader's target (Press turns every member to it, the leader included; underground the company engages `Prey`, the creature nearest the leader), and a member with no line to it takes the hostile nearest the leader (`NearestToLeader`, 355). The one exception: a member held in melee by something else answers that (`Defending`, 338), the leader too, and the company stayed on its enemy by the steady rule. Now a blow in melee on the leader turns a company that is fighting something else to what struck the leader, unless the company's enemy is itself on the leader (no turning back and forth between two blades on one leader).
- *Decision 6, responsiveness (`BotSquad.Answer`, `Tally`, `Responsiveness`, `QuickMs` 2000, `SlowMs` 10000):* nothing measured how many squad beats pass between a company engaging and its members striking. Now the first beat each member but the leader stands able to strike the company's enemy (`Strike` = Able) is counted once per member per enemy with the time since the company engaged it, filed under what the leader was doing, and at each fight's end the members still standing that never had a blow: `Companies:` "first blows on the company's enemy, by what the leader was doing when the company took it on: delve N over F fights (a mean of Xs; Q inside 2s, S past 10s; U members never had one), sweep …".

**30.09.2026 · build 340 (written by Opus, night) · A fleeing bot drops the fight that sat on top of its road; a marching leader keeps to the pace of the one behind; a hall no road reaches is met at its door; a watch inside the walls is kept; feathers go out at a gold**
- *Why (Opus's own reading of 338 and 339, `scratchpad/fleemove.py`):* each flight joined to its end and to where its bot died. On 338, 11 of the 24 fatal flights never moved a tile between "runs" and "was killed" (10 to 29 seconds), nine of them from something hand to hand one tile off (troll, ettin, ogre, giant snake); on 339's first 17 minutes, 4 of 15. Beatrix ran from a troll at (851, 1717) at 02:13:48 and was killed on that tile at 02:14:09, drinking a bottle "where it stood" in between. Flights are about half fatal whatever the foe (338: 55 % of early flights, 38 % of late; casters 47 %, hand to hand 53 %).
- *Cause:* the Will sends a deed's walk with `BotJourney.Rebase`, which keeps whatever is stacked on top (on purpose: a company's station must not wipe a fight). `BotMobile.Engage` pushes a "fight" interruption that follows its creature and lapses only when the creature dies. A bot that had squared up to a troll and then took a flight had its road away put underneath that fight: the walker served the top, the troll was beside it, Arrived; and `BotBolt` clears the combatant every beat, so the bot neither walked nor swung. `OnDamage` already refused to push a fight onto a bot in flight — the one pushed before the flight began was never taken off.
- *Decision (`BotJourney.Shed`; `BotBolt.Advance`, `Shed`):* every beat of a flight drops all interruptions from the bot's road (the fight, or a stable's "a horse" pushed mid-flight); said once per flight, "X drops its fight to run".
- *Instrument (`BotBolt.StuckMs` 4 s, `Stuck`; `BotMobile.LastWalk`):* a flight that goes four seconds without a step says so once, with the walker's last answer, the road's top errand, stamina and gait, and whether the bot is mid-spell, paralysed or frozen. No remedy is attached: whatever else holds a fleeing bot is read from these lines first.
- *Measured on 339 (02:12–02:41, 29 min):* 87 % finished (1040 of 1189), 63 killed, 30 of the deaths doing flee; journeys by purpose fixed 99.0 %, chase 99.5 %, flight 99.4 %, station 99.7 %; money +22 gp/h over the window (338: +2108; the analyst calls the first 20 minutes too volatile to compare). Chains (`night-r15-chains.md`): weaving, tinkering and brewing close; fletching does not.
- *Decision (`BotSquad.Lagging`, `Paced`; `BotBeat`):* while a member whose work is the enlistment stands further than `BotEnlist.CloseUp` (6) from a marching leader, the leader's turns come at twice its walking step. The straggler hold begins past `BotSweep.MarchSpread` (8), so a member six to eight tiles back followed the leader's body at the leader's own pace and never closed: Durgan and Morgrim "could not get one tile closer … (closing up on Liriel, company 13)" 117 times in nine minutes on 339, twelve to nineteen plans each, 2130 of the walker's cut-short searches (`night-r15-march.md`). A mounted leader goes at a footman's walk, one afoot at half of it; the member running closes.
- *Decision (`BotParley.Doorstep`, `DoorstepTiles` 16, `Doorsteps`, `Doorless`):* a town's hall whose point the gates do not join to the town's square is met at the nearest tile within 16 that they do. Britain's hall (the bank nearest its middle, beside the banker) stood at (1427, 1686) in land 7648, and 550 of 655 members asked to go to The Blade's audience were refused "no walk there". A hall is kept only once the gates are ready. Counted in the `Diplomacy:` line.

Inside the walls a watch is now held against the bidding; a flight, a mending, a rung above and what presses still take it.

Every counter prices a feather at a gold, under the 2gp `Floor`, so the kind was condemned the first time a hunter measured it; on 339 "feathers bought off a stall" stayed at 0 and arrows made at 0.

**30.09.2026 · build 339 (written by an Opus agent, merged by Opus) · The four supply chains closed: weavers walk to the flocks, tinkers and fletchers buy their input off the stalls, brewers buy the glass their herbs can fill, makers' goods reach the restock and stay under the counter's price**

- *Why (Patrick: "weavers may walk to the sheep — we don't bend the world to the bots, we make the bots smart enough to use it"; `scratchpad/agents/night-r8-money.md`; `session-2026-09-29_23-28.log`, build 336, 23:28–01:13):*
  - **What the island bought from shopkeepers in 105 minutes: 16587gp**, and 11 of the 14 largest items are things a bot makes: cloth 3773gp (1871), lesser heal + cure 3825gp (255), arrows 1568gp (784), scissors 1375gp (125, one at a time), pickaxes 968, skinning knives 647, hatchets 250. 36 of the session's 154 deaths came on a restock errand, 18 of them walking for cloth and 10 for scissors — a stall is placeless and needs no walk.
  - **Cloth.** `Needs:` 01:13 "1331 asked to weave: 332 offered a stint, 872 with no shorn sheep near, 85 with no wheel or loom within reach". The weaver asked only whether a sheep stood within 150 tiles of itself. The nine with the needle live in Britain (5), Minoc (1), Yew (3). Offline, from `Data/Spawns/shared/felucca` and the town decorations: 194 spawners raise sheep (~267 expected), none within 150 of Britain's bank (nearest single wild sheep at 192–205 tiles); the flocks are Yew's six farm spawners (~75 sheep) — and there is no wheel or loom in Yew or Minoc (the nearest to Yew's farms is Britain's, 717 tiles), which is the "85 no loom". Three more defects under it: (1) the stint's own listing never happened — "0 cloth to the market" 6 of 6 stints — because the spare was split as `new Cloth` dropped into the same pack, which `Container.TryDropItem` stacks straight back and deletes; the market refused the deleted item and the rollback added the spare again: **10 cloth created from nothing per stint over 40** (same split in `BotWeave.Bandages`, which then cut nothing whenever the pack held more cloth than it was cutting); (2) `Made` counted pieces (a bolt the counter sells for 100gp measured at 50), so the ledger priced weaving at 23–63/min against mining's median 100; (3) the cloth that did reach a stall (Berengar's, by his unload at 00:42:56) was raised to 3gp after two sales and 140 then 109 cloth stood unsold (00:46:44–00:57:06, 00:59:13–01:09:36) while 143 cloth were bought from tailors at 2 in 00:48–00:58 — `BotShopper` takes a stall only at or under the counter's price and `BotListing.Raise` never asked it.
  - **Iron → tools.** "1331 asked to tinker: 112 for the stalls, 1211 had no iron; no tinkering has ended yet". `BotTinkerer` read only its own pack; the stalls held 59–618 iron ingots at 6gp all session (15 of 21 readings over 200). The 112 offers made with iron in hand were never taken: all 26 runner-up lines lost to the forge (tinker 123–561/min, forge 288–1370). And tools would have been listed at `Worth(kind, 25)`, over the counter's 11 for scissors, 3 for a skillet.
  - **Bottles → potions.** "2630 asked to brew: 1136 had the herbs but no glass (1136 sent to buy some)", 17 brews taken. The glass leg always bought `BotFlask.Batch` = 20 bottles (100gp) though a round brews at most the cap of 5 of one draught: 61 took-on lines read "refused: brew costs 100gp and it has Ngp". Bottles in this era come from the alchemist/herbalist/provisioner at 5gp and back from every drunk potion and every failed brew (`BasePotion.PlayDrinkEffect`, `DefAlchemy.PlayEndingEffect`); there is no glassblowing. The empties already reach stalls through the unload and the leg already buys stalls first.
  - **Wood → arrows.** "740 asked to fletch: 25 on spec, 597 had no feathers and nobody sells one, 118 could not find wood". Wood: `chop` cuts only for money on the board, a fletcher of its own holding feathers, or arrows asked for — "3904 asked to cut wood: 54 sent, 3738 found nobody asking"; fletchers cannot post a want ("1259 cannot afford one, the fattest purse 116gp" against a 100gp reserve), so the first hour had no wood on any stall (the ERR line at 23:28 is said once, at the first ask). Logs reached the stalls only through gatherers' unloads, and "could not find wood" froze at 118 from 00:33. Chop's own logs go to a want first and a stall second (`BotTimber.Store`): 18 to orders, 0 to stalls. Feathers: the fletcher never looked at the stalls, which held 152–324 feathers from 00:03 to 00:38 while "no feathers" grew 147 → 336.
  - **The auction's lot cap (3 kinds a bot)** refuses a maker's fourth kind whatever it is; a crafter lists ingots, leather and blades. Not provable from the log (the refusal is counted only in total, "3250 things stayed in their sellers' hands"); instrumented below.
- *Decision:*
  - **Pastures (`BotPastures`, in `BotCraft/BotWeave.cs`).** One pass over the map's `BaseSpawner`s at the first weaver ask (the looms' rule) keeps those with a Sheep entry; readiness is the engine's own `NextWoolTime`, not the body (which only a running AI refreshes, and the far flocks sleep). A pasture a weaver found shorn rests until its soonest regrowth, 10 min to 3 h.
  - **`BotWeaver`** weighs every pasture within `PastureReach` 600 of the weaver and inside its leash, on its land, not refused, not perilous (`BotGround.MineOdds`, the woods' test), not sealed, with a wheel and loom within `BotWeave.LoomReach`, by **road to the flock + road on to the loom, per sheep ready** (up to a full stint). `LoomReach` 400 → **800** so Yew's farms can be woven at Britain. The stint's `Where` is the pasture, so the walk is priced by the auction like any other; wool target up to `WoolAfield` 10 (6 bolts, ~300 cloth); `AfieldCapMs` 30 min; `Bend` tries another sheep three times then marks the pasture.
  - **`BotWeave`**: splits with `Mobile.LiftItemDupe` in the listing and in `Bandages` (the dup is gone); `Made` in gold (`Worth(Cloth, 2)`, `Worth(Bandage, 5)`); cloth over `BotSew.Bolt × 2` goes to an order, then a stall at `max(Floor, min(Worth, the nearest tailor's price))`.
  - **`BotTinkerer` / `BotTinker`**: short of iron, the stint's first leg buys a batch and a miss (`cost × (Batch + 1)`, at least `LeastMetal`) off the cheapest stall — placeless, priced as `Outlay`, skipped and counted (`Poor`) when the purse cannot carry it; steadfast once it has bought. Tools listed at `max(Floor, min(Worth, the nearest shopkeeper's price))`.
  - **`BotAlchemist.Glassware`**: glass sized to what the herbs can fill for the chosen draught under its cap (`BotFlask.GlassFor`), at least `LeastBottles` 5, at most `Batch` 20, cut to what the purse carries; below one draught's glass it is counted (`Unaffordable`).
  - **`BotFletcher` / `BotFletch`**: with no feathers, a round buys up to 20 off the cheapest stall holding ≥ `LeastFeathers` 5 as its first leg, wood matched to them as before. A fletcher that finds no feathers anywhere, or no wood anywhere, raises a ten-minute call (`Starved`, `Woodless`): **`BotWoodsman`** cuts for the stalls while it stands and the stalls hold under 40 logs (non-fletching cutters list everything they cut); **`BotQuarry.Sought`** reads `Starved` as it reads a feather want (the bird bounty).
  - **`BotAuction.MadeUncapped`** (on): `List(…, made: true)` from the weaver, tinker, brewer and fletcher goes out past `LotsPerBot`, counted (`PastCap`). Loot and porters' loads are capped as before.
  - **`BotAuction.CounterCeiling`** (on): a brisk seller's raise stops at `BotShops.Lowest(kind)` — the least any known shopkeeper asks, cached 5 min; kinds no shopkeeper sells are raised as before (`HeldAtCounter`). `BotListing.Raise` gains the ceiling overload.
  - Resets: `BotCraftModule.Reset` now forgets the looms, pastures, weaver and tinker counters on a world reload (the looms and pastures hold world references).
- *Measured offline:* build 0 errors 0 warnings; the patch applies to a fresh copy of base336 and to the live tree's current files (all 15 identical to base336). Pasture geometry from the spawn files and decorations: at the old rule Britain had no pasture within 150; now Britain has 40 pastures (~1 sheep each) within 600 with a loom in reach, Minoc 25, Yew 25 (~71 sheep, the farms at cost 167 road-tiles per sheep, the best on the island); at `LoomReach` 400 Yew had 2. Glass: of the 61 "brew costs 100gp" refusals, 26 brewers held ≥ 25gp (a 5-bottle batch) and 33 ≥ 10gp. Tinker iron per stint 48–96gp: the three architects (3209–6623gp) can buy any batch, Aldric (57) and Amberle (100) the two-ingot tools, the others none. Cloth demand ≈ 1130/h (1871 bought + 103 off stalls in 105 min); the ~130 sheep within the three weaver towns' reach (the sets overlap a little) regrow ≈ 2100 cloth/h at fifty cloth a sheep every three hours — if weavers reach them and hunters leave them.
- *Not verified (needs a run):* that the spawners exist in the live world and are surveyed (boot line `Pastures:`); that weavers win the auction for a 200–700 tile walk and survive it; that a Yew weaver walks to Britain's loom; that tinkers are ever chosen over the forge (the forge competition is untouched); that fletching from bought wood and feathers is chosen (a log at 2–3 and a feather at 1–3 against an arrow at 2 loses money, and the ledger will learn that); how often the lot cap bit.
- *Watch (session log, cumulative — diff the 5-minute summaries):*
  - boot: `Supplies from our own benches: … past the auction's lot cap: True`; first weaver ask: `Pastures: N spawners on Felucca raise sheep, keeping M now, K of them with their wool grown`;
  - `Needs:` weaving — "N offered a stint (A to a flock past 150 tiles, T tiles off on average)", "no flock they could get to", the pasture buckets (shorn / let be / leash / land / refused / perilous / no way / no loom), and "S weaving stints ended (… sent past 150 …) … C cloth put out (O to orders, U the market would not take)"; per stint `X sheared W wool, wove B bolts … N cloth to the market at 2gp`;
  - `Needs:` tinker — "(B of them to buy their iron off a stall first)", "P could not pay…", "I iron bought off the stalls"; per stint `X tinkered N Scissors … to the market at 11gp, out of K iron bought off the stalls`;
  - `Needs:` brew — "S sent to buy some, N bottles between them" (the average should be ~5, not 20), "U could not pay for the glass their herbs could fill";
  - `Needs:` fletch — "(F of them buying their feathers off a stall, P feathers bought so)"; `The ground:` "(S of them because a fletcher went without wood …)";
  - `The market:` "… and P their makers put out past it; H brisk sellers' raises held at the shopkeeper's price";
  - the money: `bought N Cloth|Scissors|LesserHealPotion|Arrow from` per hour against the 105-minute baseline above (3773 / 1375 / 2280 / 1568gp), `off the market` purchases of the same kinds, and deaths `died doing restock: after N Cloth`.
- *Open (§6, for Patrick):*
  1. **Yew's weavers carry their wool to Britain.** `LoomReach` 800 makes the largest flocks usable; the alternative is a loom in Yew (bending the world, which you ruled out), or weavers never using Yew's flocks. Keep 800?
  2. **Anyone with scissors could weave.** Shearing, spinning, the loom and cutting need no skill; only the nine with the needle are asked. The 16 gatherers already walk the countryside. Open weaving to gatherers?
  3. **Hunters kill the flocks.** 28 sheep were killed on hunts in 105 minutes (19 carved for two things each); a wild spawner puts back a sheep one time in nineteen, so each kill near a town is that pasture's wool gone. Spare sheep while cloth is short, or leave it to the hunt's pricing?
  4. **The forge outbids the tinker for the same iron, every time.** Tools are worth 3–25gp and blades 45+, so by the ledger's measure the anvil is right; but the island buys ~2000gp/h of tools over counters. Price tinkering for a tool the shops' book shows the island buying as an order (×1.6), or let it be?
  5. **`CounterCeiling` applies to every kind a shopkeeper sells**, loot included (reagents, ingots). Narrow it to the makers' kinds?
  6. **Fletching from bought wood and feathers loses money** at today's prices; the self-sufficient arrow is the fletcher's own wood (it carries a hatchet) and a hunter's feathers. Leave the ledger to learn it?

**30.09.2026 · build 339 (written by an Opus agent, merged by Opus) · The company stands to a fight on the road; a member hit and losing may run and mend; the party is counted before the mouth and turns back together; a gate that puts a walker down above the floor sets it on the floor**

- *What 336 wrote on Durgan's march to the Orc Caves (01:01:38–01:10:56, `session-2026-09-29_23-28.log`):* five marched from (1487, 1007). 01:06:07 "Squad 261 of 5 is dealing with a reaper (3740)"; 01:06:10 "Helja runs early at 41 of 75 health … (0 of ours near), from a reaper (a caster, 1 tiles off)" — twice, and no flight taken; 01:06:17 "Helja died doing enlist" at (1100, 998). 01:06:34 Dagna "runs at 25 of 75" (Failing rung), no flight, three bottles; 01:07:49 "Durgan leaves Dagna behind … 24 tiles back after 90s — holding enlist … journey active, not moving towards (1088, 995, 0) (sweep)" — a scouting patch the company's own scatter had sent her to while the leader held. 01:09:58–01:10:27 the company of three changed focus twelve times (Peghed, a gazer, Peghed, the gazer, Ckukchik, the gazer, an ogre, the gazer, the ogre, a gazer, another ogre, the gazer) at (1021, 1395), 39 tiles short of the mouth; Norbert and Thalion "run early" at 44–46 and 37–38 of 67, no flight taken; Thalion "died doing enlist" at 01:10:28 (a ratman), Norbert at 01:10:33 (an ogre). Durgan, the only one left living, "has led 1 into the Orc Caves by its mouth" 23 seconds later; the delve ended at 01:12:56 "there was nobody left to delve with". Where Durgan stood during either fight is not in the log; the march does one of two things on every beat — walks to the mouth, or holds (`Journey.Finish`) — and both cancel the station a fighting company gives its leader.
- *What 336–337 wrote on the sweeps:* all three that "came apart" came apart in a fight the captain walked away from — Squad 7 on a plague spawn at 23:34:53, "Aelith leaves Galathil behind … 113 tiles back after 26s … journey active, not moving towards (1526, 769, 0) (station)"; Squad 136 on a wraith at 00:14:22, Helja and Liesl left at 62 and 61 (station); Squad 36 on two wraiths at 01:28:57–01:29:27 ("we never got near it — nearest 11 tiles off"), Dagna left at 115 (station). Members at their places round the enemy; the captain marching on; the straggler rule counting the gap.
- *Why (four holes, all in code that each worked alone):*
  1. **The leader's march never looked at the company's stance.** `BotDelve.Marching` and `BotSweep.March` answered the walk (or a hold that finishes the journey) on every beat while the company fought; the Baron's harrowing learned the opposite on 16.09 (`BotHarrow`, "while the company is on something, the leader answers Work and is stationed and pressed like everybody else") and the two marches were written without it.
  2. **A member holding its enlistment could neither run nor bind a wound.** `BotEnlist.Committed` (309) keeps an enlistment from being bid away, and its note says "a rescue or a flight still jumps it"; only `Pressing` work gets past a committed deed in `BotWill.Auction`, and neither `BotBolt` nor `BotSalve` is pressing, so the survival rungs' offers were `Kept` out. Since 333 began writing every flight down, 7 of the 8 deaths "doing enlist" (Amberle 22:19, Harald, Caelynn, Norbert 23:57, Helja, Thalion, Norbert 01:10) had "runs … at N of M health" said for them in the forty seconds before, and none took flight; of the day's 36 deaths "doing band" — the band is not committed — 24 had taken flight first.
  3. **In a fight the close-up walked members to the leader, away from the fight.** In the fighting stance the anchor is the creature; `BotEnlist.Holding` walked any member further than `CloseUp` (6) from it to the leader's body — every caster and healer (their place is seven out), every archer shooting from further than six, and with a leader marching on, out of the fight.
  4. **A holding leader turned the company into a scouting party.** `BotSquad.Settle` reads a leader with no walk in hand as arrived on empty ground (Scouting) and scatters the members to patches (`BotScatter`) — on the march that is every hold. And a marching sweep's company hunted at `BotMuster.Reach` (120) of its captain.
