**29.09.2026 · build 3xx (written by an Opus agent) · No war without a meeting: envoys, a witness, the duke's word; agreements between guilds; guilds and their towns**
- *Why (Patrick's order of 29.09.2026, evening, four points):* (1) a guild may declare war on another only at a meeting in the main building of a town on the host's ground — The Blade's envoy walks to Cove to talk to The Needle there — with one of the debuggers invited as a visible witness who hears both sides; the meeting may end in agreement or in war; "this removes lightning decisions and gives time for the guilds' work"; the decider is prompted "you are the duke of this land; your vassals quarrel over land …"; (2) alliances, orders, trade and safety are agreed the same way; (3) a guild deals with its town: the debugger reports the town's state and sets a unique task, each success −0.5 % on that town's prices for the guild, each failure +0.5 %, three failures in a row and the guild is put out of the town for a couple of days; (4) the envoy is any member, a guild of one sends its founder. Until now `BotRegard.Reckon` declared a war the instant an opinion crossed `Enmity` and `BotWar.MayDeclare` allowed it, and made an alliance the instant both opinions crossed `Alliance`; nothing walked, nothing was said, and no town had a word to say to anybody.
- *Found on the way (live session 20:38, build 326):* `Estate:` reads "42 opinions between guilds, worst nobody thinks ill of anybody … 0 wars declared" and every guild's treasury is 0 of 5000; `bot-estate.json` runs the war line at −100 with `TruceMinutes` 0, `DeclareEveryMinutes` 0 and `MostWars` 3. So on the day's world a grievance meeting is rare at first, and the town audiences are what will be seen first (within 20 minutes of a boot).
- *Decision (`BotDiplomacy/`, new folder, module `Diplomacy`, `Configuration/bot-diplomacy.json`, starter written empty):*
  - **Meetings (`BotParley`, `BotHearing`).** `BotRegard.Reckon` and `BotRegard.Drift` call `BotParley.Grieve` where they declared (after `MayDeclare`, which is asked again at the verdict); `Reckon` calls `BotParley.Befriend` where it allied. Both return false only when the module is off or not yet started, so the old path is kept intact behind them. A meeting is also called by the module's own look (once a minute, at most one call a look, `CallOdds` 0.2 per eligible pair): a guild the other thinks ill of (≤ `Enmity × WaryShare`, −50 on the live line) goes to ask for peace; two guilds both ≥ `Cordial` (25) — the smaller proposing — go to agree trade. At most `MostMeetings` 2 between guilds and `MostAudiences` 2 with towns at once (the squad is four). A pair is not called again for `MeetEveryMs` 2 h after an agreement or a war, `RetryMs` 30 min after nothing or a lapse; a grievance crossing the line meanwhile waits (`Standing`), and a pair already meeting waits (`Pending`). No war is declared anywhere else; wars already standing and allies joining a war (`BotWar.Enlist`) are untouched.
  - **Where (`BotParley.Seat`, `BotParley.Hall`).** The host's town is the town nearest its seat (`BotSeat.Of`: hand, file, founding, or its hall) within `SeatTownTiles` 300, else where most of its members live (`BotResidence`), else home; the place is that town's main building: `Halls` in the file by town name, else the bank beside the banker (`BotSettle.Amenities.Hearth`), else the square (Cove has no bank). **This is the one function the guild-house patch should teach to answer with a house's door.** A guest whose home no walk joins to the place (`BotGates.Joined`) is not called (`Unreachable`, pair clock 30 min) — so guilds with no walk between them cannot go to war.
  - **Who (`BotHerald` → `BotEnvoy` "envoy", Free rung, unpaid, steadfast, `Prior` 150/min).** Offered to every free member of the guest guild (a guild of one: its founder) that is alive, not tired, not in a company or underground, not red or grey (guards), fit (`BotHunter.FitAt`), with a walk joined to the place and not sealed (`BotReach`); the first to take it holds it in `Taken` (DECISIONS A7) and renews the hold each beat (`ClaimMs` 3 min); a member that dies, rests or is taken off lets another go; one the road beat is not asked again (`Turned`). The host guild is asked for an answerer once the envoy is within `HostCallTiles` 150. The errand is held for its walk plus ten minutes (`HoldsFor`), committed and `Still` once at the place, fails after `MarchMs` 30 min on the road, finishes when the word was given and fails when the meeting lapsed — so it counts honestly in the finished share. A mage with a rune recalls (`BotRecall.Instead`).
  - **The witness (`mindedBots/debugger/BotWitness`, three hooks `BotParley.Summon/Dismiss/Judge` filled in `BotDebugModule.Start`).** When the envoy is there, a free watcher (the lead unless it is charting the dungeons, then the helpers, the marshal last) is `Hover`ed two tiles off the place and `Hidden = false`; `BotVigil.Follow` does not move a watcher that `BotWitness.Busy`; at the end it is hidden again (and `Hover` re-hides it on any move). Blessed and above Player it stays out of every fight while seen (`CanBeHarmful`; `BaseAI.AcquireFocusMob` skips blessed and staff). No witness free in `WitnessWaitMs` 3 min, or no debugger loaded: the meeting goes on unwitnessed and the envoy relays the word.
  - **The hearing and the duke (`BotDuke`, `BotGrievances`).** `BotRegard.Move` now also writes each move into a per-pair book under its cause ("working our land", "refusing to move along", "claiming our ground", "blood", "a shared border", "trade", "a corpse shared", "help …"; not "time"), closed by `BotRegard.Settle`. Lines, five seconds apart (`LineMs`), from the phrase bank (`parley:*`, defaults registered for keys `bot-voice.json` lacks): the witness opens, the envoy states its two worst causes (or its best, when proposing), the host answers from its own book (or the witness says nobody came, after `HostWaitMs` 4 min), the witness says the duke will weigh it. The duke is asked at the opening through the one Ollama slot (`BotOllama`, `JudgeModel` empty = the population's qwen3.5:9b, `JudgeKeepAlive` "10s", `JudgeTimeoutMs` 90 s) with Patrick's framing in English, the brief from the books, opinions, might, towns, land, halls, wars, allies and what was said, and a schema whose outcome is an enumeration narrowed per topic (`Allowed`: grievance → war, peace, trade, orders; safety → peace, trade, orders, nothing; friendship → alliance (only with room), trade, orders, nothing; commerce → trade, orders, nothing) with `minLength` floors on speech and reason. No readable answer in `JudgeWaitMs` 2 min after the last line: the rule (`BotDuke.Rule`) reads the same books — blood, a claim on the hall's ground, a grievance both ways, or a host that would not come is war; a quarrel between guilds that traded ≥ `TradesForTerms` 3 times is trade; otherwise peace. A late answer is counted and dropped.
  - **What each word does (`BotDuke.Apply`, `BotPact`), each changing one real thing.** *War*: `MayDeclare` asked again, then `BotWar.Declare` (allies join as before). *Peace*: `BotRegard.Settle` both ways and a truce in the war ledger for `PactHours` 12 (`BotWar.RestoreTruce`), which `MayDeclare` already refuses on. *Trade*: for 12 h a member buys off the other guild's stalls at `TradeDiscount` 10 % off — `BotAuction.Cheapest` compares the price this buyer would pay and `BotAuction.Buy` charges it; the seller is paid the same lower bill, so no coin is created. *Orders*: for 12 h `BotAuction.Demand` serves a partner guild's want before a stranger's of the same kind, whatever either pays. Trade and orders also settle a grievance or a safety quarrel. *Alliance*: the engine's `AddAlly`. Agreements are kept across restarts as time left.
  - **Towns (`BotBurgh`, `BotTownTask`, `BotTownReport`).** Each guild deals with its seat's town and every town where ≥ `LeastResidents` 3 of its members live, one audience at a time, first one within `FirstMs` 20 min of a boot, then `EveryMs` 1 h after each task ends. The envoy walks to the town's hall; the witness speaks for the town: its shops (those `BotShops` knows in its box) and which of the island's shortages (`BotShops.Dry`) none of them has on the shelf, the market's board, the squares within `TownReach` 90 of the hall reading unsafe and the dead in them, the residents, the guild's standing. Task catalogue, all checked by code once a minute: **clear** — the worst unsafe square near the hall whose muscle × `ClearOdds` 2 the guild's might covers, to read `ClearGain` 0.1 better (up to neutral) with `ClearPresence` 10 member-minutes stood in it; **guard** — `GuardMinutes` 90 member-minutes inside the walls; **supply-<material>** — `SupplyUnits` 20 of the material the market is shortest of put on stalls or into orders by members (counted in `BotAuction.List` and `BotAuction.Fill`). A square or material another guild is working for the same town is not offered (unique). The model picks the task and says the report and the charge (task id is an enumeration); by rule: clear, else supply, else guard. The guild is charged as a price, never a command: a `BotCharter` muster at the square or hall while its charter is empty, or a request on its board for the material every 20 min. Deadline `TaskHours` 2 h. Done: that town's prices for that guild −`PriceStep` 0.5 %; failed +0.5 %; clamped `LeastFactor` 0.90 … `MostFactor` 1.10; `FailsToExile` 3 in a row: put out for `ExileHours` 48 wall-clock hours.
  - **The price (`BotShops.Buy`).** The factor of the buyer's guild in the town the shop stands in: affordability judged at the dearer price; after the engine's own `OnBuyItems` the difference is handed back into the bank (never more than that purchase paid — every purchase still takes coin out of the world, only less) or taken on top through `BotAuction.Charge`. `BotShops.Price` (estimates) is left at the shelf.
  - **Put out (`BotBurgh.Bars`).** `BotSettle.Choose` passes the town over for the guild's members, `BotRelocate.Forced` no longer forces them there, `BotRelocate.Judge` marks a member living there to move at once (as from a town not fit to live in), and a guild seated by that town is seated by the reachable fit town with the fewest seats that has not put it out (`ExileMovesSeat`, `BotSeat.Set(…, false)`; a hall is then carried by the estate's own errand).
  - **Kept across restarts (`BotDiplomacyStore` "BotDiplomacy", shape 1):** agreements and pair clocks as time left, the books, and every non-trivial standing with its task (time left); exile as a UTC date. Meetings in flight are not kept.
- *Also:* the `Diplomacy:` summary line after `Wars:` (`BotBeat`), `The debugger:` line gains the witness's counts; `"diplomacy"` on the web snapshot (relations with opinions, agreements and both books; each guild's standing in its towns with the task; meetings standing; the last endings) and a "Diplomacy" list under Squads on the page; events `parley` on the stream; Argus's door: `do parley`, `do meet <guild> ; <guild or town> [; topic]` (hand verbs), and `reset` wipes the diplomacy stores; `regen-map.py` knows the folder (MAP §2 block and DIALS rows inserted by hand from a scratch regeneration, because a full regeneration also rewrites unrelated stale rows).
- *Measured before deploying:* one ask to the live Ollama with the real prompt and schema (a Blade–Needle grievance with six refusals and one death): qwen3.5:9b answered in 27.5 s from cold, `{"outcome":"peace", "speech":"The Blade and The Needle shall wipe their grievances …", "reason":"…"}` — the schema and the enumeration hold. Build: 0 errors, 0 warnings. Nothing else is measured: the shard was not run.
- *Watch:*
  - boot: `Diplomacy is on: no war and no alliance without a meeting at the host's town; 2 meetings between guilds and 2 with towns at a time, …`; the store: `Diplomacy: N agreements, … read back from the save` from the second boot;
  - `<Guest> calls a meeting with <Host> over a grievance (…): its envoy is to walk to <Town> at x,y`, then `<Name> the <Class> of <Guest> sets out as envoy`, `<Name> is witness to meeting #N at <Town>` (session log) and `… is summoned as witness … shows itself` (bot-debugger.log), `Meeting #N: … are heard at <Town> before <Witness>; the word may be …, and is asked of the model`, `Meeting #N: … — the word, by the model|the rule (…), is <outcome>: "<speech>"`; the model's own line in bot-debugger.log;
  - towns: `<Guild> sends an envoy to <Town>'s hall …`, `<Guild> has done|failed <Town>'s task (…): its prices there are ×0.995 now`, `<Town> has put <Guild> out after 3 failed tasks …` (also an `exile` alarm), `<Guild>, put out of <Town>, is seated by <Other>`;
  - the `Diplomacy:` line: called by topic, heard / witnessed / unwitnessed / host absent, lapsed for want of an envoy, verdicts by model and by rule with late and unreadable answers, wars at a meeting and refused at the word, envoys set out / arrived / finished / lapsed / unreached / replaced, the herald's refusals, agreements and their use on the market, and the towns' clause (tasks by kind, done, failed, exiles, rebates and surcharges, units supplied);

- *Open (§6):*
  1. **War is only ever declared at a meeting now, including through the rule.** A host that sends nobody in four minutes gets war by rule; a guest that cannot walk to the host's town can never declare. Keep both, or should an unreachable host be met at the guest's town?
  2. **Is the witness the duke's voice, or should the duke be somebody else?** Built as: the witness (one of the squad) hears, and says the model's word as "the duke's word"; with no witness the envoy relays it.
  3. **Town tasks are prices, not orders** (a `BotCharter` muster or a board request, ×1.5). A guild that never takes them up will fail three in a row and be put out within about six hours of its first audience. Too harsh at `TaskHours` 2 and `EveryMs` 1 h? The guard task is easy for a guild that already lives in the town.
  4. **Exile moves the seat** (`ExileMovesSeat` on). For a guild with a hall this carries the hall; turn off if a seat should only follow a war.
  5. **Supply is counted when goods go out** (listed or filled), so goods taken off a stall and listed again count twice. Count sales instead (slower, cannot be gamed)?
  6. **Who pays the rebate.** It is the engine's own coin handed back out of what that purchase paid (a smaller sink), not minted beyond it; the city's treasury (`BotCity`) could pay it instead if the sink must stay whole.
  7. **One alliance per guild (`BotRegard.MostAllies` 1)** still binds a sworn alliance; and an alliance sworn at a meeting is still ended by `BotRegard` below `Estrangement` without a meeting.

**29.09.2026 · build after 326 (written by an Opus agent) · Bots' shops by the bank; the auction cut to three kinds a bot**
- *Why (Patrick's order of the evening):* "move away from the internal auction by degrees; bots keep shops by the bank or their own storage and call out to the bots that need their goods; later a merchant caste; for now don't remove the auction, just cut the lots a bot may have".
- *What existed (17:38–18:38 on 29.09, 35 bots, one hour):*
  - **The auction held 184 stalls with 441 things (2018gp).** The sellers whose prices moved held up to 11 kinds each; 17 of those 33 sellers held more than 3.
  - **The auction's trade:** 199 sales and 171 fills came to 7961gp. 291 things crossed straight from a stall to a want. The board held 43 wants for 329 things, with 3017gp in escrow; 126 wants were posted in the hour.
  - **The city bought 2795gp off stalls in 129 lots.** That is the only outside buyer.
  - **Supplies (`restock`, 265 finished):** 210 were bought over a shopkeeper's counter, 55 off a stall and 0 at a guild's counter. The shopkeepers took 6385gp for 1582 things. The biggest items were cloth (672 for 1344gp), sulfurous ash (320, 960gp), lesser heal potions (61, 915gp) and arrows (275, 550gp). The stalls supplied 81 ash, 42 pearl, 20 cure potions and 60 cloth.
  - **Peddling to shopkeepers:** 53 loads for 2780gp.
  - **Fills by value:** leather chests 982gp, leather 814gp (152), iron ingots 387gp, raw ribs 327gp (127).
  - No bot stood anywhere to trade. A town was not a place where trade happened.
- *Decision (`BotShopkeep/`, new, module `Shopkeep`, `Configuration/bot-botshops.json`):* a bot sells from its own pack and bank box, standing beside the bank nearest home. There are eight files.
  - `BotShopkeeper` (proposer):
    - counts the bot's goods the way the porter counts them. That is the bank box whole, plus the pack over `BotUnload.Keeps`. It never includes bound things, coin, containers, keys, runes, runebooks, spellbooks, ship or house deeds, the bot's own kit items, or a kind it has a want out for.
    - prices each kind at the nearest shopkeeper's ask, or `BotAuction.Worth` when that is less. Never above the shelf and never under `Floor`.
    - offers a shift when the part the island is asking for comes to `OpenWorth` (80gp) or more. "Asking for" means `BotShopper.Shortages` or an open want.
    - claims the shift at that demanded worth × the sell-through ÷ `ShiftMinutes`. The sell-through starts at `SellShare` 0.5 and becomes the measured share after `LeastShifts` 5 shifts. The claim is clamped to 2…120/min, and the ledger corrects it per bank.
    - outlaws are refused. So are bots with no banker within `BankTiles` 80 of `BotPopulation.HomeOf`, and banks already at `PerBank` 4 shops. The whole island is capped at `MostOpen` 16.
  - `BotKeepShop` (deed `shopkeep`):
    - walks to a pitch 2–6 tiles from the banker, on its floor, `Apart` 2 from other shops. The pitch is spoken for from `Taken`, so bots choosing in one step after a boot do not all pick one bank's last place.
    - opens, calls out (`BotVoice`, "shop:open"/"shop:cry" every `CryMs` 45s, rationed again by the voice), and serves.
    - shuts when the goods are gone or after `ShiftMinutes` 8. It is `Still` once open and `Steadfast` throughout. When put down for what will not wait, the shop shuts while the keeper is away and reopens when it is back. The shift's clock counts open minutes only.
    - is finished either way ("sold out" / "the shift is over", the latter including "nobody came to buy"). It fails when the pitch cannot be reached (filed under `shopkeep` at the pitch, which `Pitch` avoids next time), when the bank will not take another shop, or when the goods were gone on arrival. Takings are measured as coin (`Coin` 1, `Made` 0, the peddler's arithmetic).
  - `BotShopkeep.Beats` (supplies):
    - `BotShopper` asks it before its stall/counter choice. The shop wins when its landed price is no more than the shopkeeper's landed price and no more than the cheapest stall. The shop's landed price is its ask plus the walk to it, at `WalkGold` a minute (following `BotRestock.Prior`, 12) at the appraisal's walking pace (`BotAppraisal.Travel`). The shopkeeper's landed price is his price plus his walk. The stall has no walk.
    - Ties go to the shop. With no shop open nothing changes.
  - `BotPatron` (wants):
    - a bot with an open want is offered the walk when a shop's landed price is at or under the want's offer.
    - At the till, the escrow is taken back (`BotAuction.Withdrawn`) and the goods are bought at the keeper's price. What the shop could not supply is asked for again at the same offer.
  - The customer's walk is `BotRestock`'s fourth source, not a new trade: unpaid, `restock`, steadfast.
    - It follows the keeper within `ServeReach` 3.
    - A shop that shut or sold out sends a supplies errand on to the nearest shopkeeper (`FellThrough`, as the guild's bare shelf does).
    - `AtCounter` is true for it (a full pack is refused first). `Outlay` is 0 for a want's walk, because its money is on the board.
  - The till (`Serve`) follows the auction's order:
    1. Charge the buyer (`BotAuction.Charge`, pack then account, all or nothing).
    2. Move the goods from the keeper's bank box, then its pack, into the buyer's pack. Stacks are split with `Mobile.LiftItemDupe`, and the drop is `TryDropItem`.
    3. Refund what did not move, into the account.
    4. Pay the keeper for what moved, as `Gold` into its pack. The account takes it when the pack will not, and the pack takes it regardless when neither will.

    The quoted price is honoured if the ask rose while the buyer walked. No levy.
  - Prices move by the auction's own numbers:
    - up `RaiseStep` when a kind sells again inside `BriskMs`;
    - down `CutStep` for each kind nobody bought during a shift that ran at least half its length;
    - inside `LeastMultiple`…`MostMultiple` of the opening.

    `BotShopkeep.PriceFor(front, buyer, kind)` is the one place the price a buyer pays is read. It is the seam for a guild's factor in a town (the diplomacy agent) or a merchant's margin.
  - At the bank the keeper first tops its own pack up to its keep list out of its own box (`SelfSupply`, counted). The porter's `Store` puts surplus there and nothing ever took it out, so otherwise a shop would sell its keeper's bandages while the keeper bought more from a shopkeeper.
  - `BotShopBook` (the merchant's seam): per town and kind, what bots bought at bots' shops (units, gold, last price), what they bought from shopkeepers (the same, booked from `BotRestock`), and customers who came and found none.
- *Decision (`BotAuction.LotsPerBot`, `Capped`):* a new kind past the limit is refused in `List` before the sign flips and before anything moves.
  - Topping up a stall already out is unaffected.
  - Every caller already leaves a refused thing where it was. The porter then puts it in the bank box (`BotUnload.Store`) and the shop sells it from there. Nothing is destroyed.
  - The code default is 0 (no cap). `BotShopkeepModule` sets it from `AuctionLots` (3), and to 0 when the shops are off, because a cap with no shop only fills bank boxes. It is live through the door as `dial BotAuction.LotsPerBot N`.
  - `The market:` gains "N things stayed in their sellers' hands for want of a lot, at 3 kinds a bot".
- *Decision (`BotHerbs.Scarcest` reads `BotShopkeep.Showing` too):* with the cap, a picker's fourth reagent never reaches a stall. Read off the stalls alone it would look scarce for ever and be picked into the picker's own bank box. What an open shop shows now counts; a bank box between shifts does not.
- *Hooks in shared files (all commented):*
  - `BotCore`: register the module.
  - `BotAuction.List`: the cap, plus `Capped` and the clause on its line.
  - `BotShopper.Propose`: `Beats` before the stall and counter, and "N to a bot's shop by the bank" on its line.
  - `BotRestock`: the constructor, the `Advance` branch, `Bend`, `AtCounter`, `Outlay`, and `BotShopBook.Counter` after a shopkeeper purchase.
  - `BotHerbs.Scarcest`.
  - `BotWebSnapshot`: `shops`.
  - `BotPhrases`: `shop:open`, `shop:cry`, `shop:sold`, `shop:close`.
  - The page: a `shops` layer.
  - `regen-map.py`, `MAP.md` §1 and §2, `DIALS.md`.
- *Watch:*
  - **Boot:** "Bots' shops are open: … the auction takes at most 3 kinds from one bot", then "Proposer Shopkeeper …" and "Proposer Patron …".
  - **A shift:** "X took on shopkeep: going to the bank at (x, y) to keep shop with Ngp of goods the island is asking for: N/min = …". Then "X opened a shop by the bank at (x, y) in <town>: …", "X shut its shop in <town> after N minutes: …" and "X finished shopkeep: the shift is over: sold N things to M customers for Ngp …".
  - **A sale:** "X bought N <kind> at Y's shop in <town> for Ngp, P each — short of it for its kit" or "— against its own want on the board"; "X finished restock: … at Y's shop …".
  - **Summaries:**
    - `Bot shops:` — shifts, sales by need, supplies weighed and won or lost, the patron's looks, the till, prices, sell-through, the auction's cap and the book.
    - `The market:` — the stall count against 184 at the same age, and `Capped`.
    - `Trade:` — "N things bought for Ngp" (shopkeepers) against the shops' takings.
    - `Resolve:` — shopkeep's finished share.
  - **The page:** the `shops` layer.
- *Not verified:* nothing has run on a shard.
  - It builds with 0 errors and 0 warnings on the build 325 snapshot, and on a fresh copy of the snapshot with the patch applied, and on a copy of the live sources taken at 21:40 with the guild-house patch merged.
  - The patch applies to a fresh copy of the snapshot. Against the live tree one hunk fails: `regen-map.py`'s `ORDER`, because the guild-house patch changed the next line. Add `"BotShopkeep"` after `"BotAuction"` by hand.
  - Unknown until it runs:
    - whether pitches at the banks are reachable and on the right floor;
    - whether a shift's claim ever wins over real work (it is priced to lose to production and beat an idle prowl);
    - how often customers find a shop sold out.
- *Status:* **attempt**.

**Open questions for Patrick**
1. **The levy.** The market's keeper (the Architect) takes 1% of every auction sale. Bot shops pay nothing, and as the auction shrinks so does the Architect's income. Should shops pay it too?
2. **The city.** It bought 2795gp of goods off stalls in one hour on 17:38. It is the only outside buyer, and goods the cap sends to the bank are invisible to it. Should it buy from open shops as well, or send its standing orders to them?
3. **Which three lots.** A bot keeps the first three kinds it lists; a stall only leaves the board when sold out or taken back after 30 minutes at its lowest ask. Should a bot hand back its worst-selling lot when a better kind arrives, so its three lots are its best goods?
4. **Guild halls and houses as shop sites.** For now a shop stands only at a bank. That is neutral ground, and the bank box is "its own storage". Once the guild buildings in towns settle, should a member keep shop at its guild's door, selling the guild's stock?
5. **The keeper and the board.** A keeper at the bank could fill wants on the board straight from its bank box, placeless, as the porter fills them from a pack. Now only the patron walks to the keeper. Is that the shape you want?
6. **Shop prices in the shard's reckoning.** `BotAuction.Worth`, which producers count their output at, reads stalls and bids only. Should the shops' book feed it?
7. **The next step, the merchant caste.** A class or office that:
   - reads `BotShopBook` for a town and kind with a large "from shopkeepers" column and few bots' shops, or with "came and found none";
   - buys that kind where it is cheap (a shopkeeper's shelf, another shop, a stall);
   - stores it in its bank box;
   - carries it to the town that needs it (`BotTravel` roads);
   - keeps shop there.

   The shop, the till, the pitch and the book already exist; what is missing is the buying to resell and the carrying. Should it be a class (like the Captain), an office any bot takes (like the guild's supplier), or a guild of merchants?

**29.09.2026 · build 330 (written by Opus, night) · A dungeon is not a road; a weapon is worth its wielder's skill; one death is one death; a walker that thrashes stops**
- *Measured on 329 (21:06–21:17):* 365 of 459 endings finished (80 %), 37 failed, 16 dropped, 41 died — the night's worst ten minutes. Homeward 50 % with 39 % dropped; flee 47 %. The first night analysts (Sonnet, read-only, `scratchpad/agents/night-*-1.md`) over 20:16–21:18: 44 % of deaths within a median 13 s of "took on flee"; 20 bots made 70 % of the deaths (Sigurd six times, four of them alone at 315 of strength); 56 of 151 "died doing" lines were echoes of a death already counted; one bot's walk loop made 601 of the fixed-goal path failures.
- *Decision (`BotGates.First`, `DungeonToll` 3000, `Toll`; route cache keyed by the lands and the 64-tile squares of start and goal; Argus `gates route x1 y1 x2 y2`):* Gimrund and Edmund, sent home to The Crown's new house in Skara Brae, went in by the mouth of Despise and stood at (5573, 632) for eight minutes ("the walk stopped closing 5014 tiles short"): the gates were weighed by straight distance, a cave as cheap as a road, moongates read from the whole map stand inside dungeons too, and one walker's first gate was handed to every walker of the land for a minute. A gate that sets the walker down inside a dungeon other than the one it is bound for now costs 3000 tiles more, and the cached answer is the answer for that start and goal.
- *Decision (`BotThreat.AverageDamage`, `SkillWeighs`, `SkillFloor` 0.25):* a wielder's weapon damage is taken at (skill + 20) / 120 of itself — the era's hit chance grows with the attacker's skill — so a master reads as before and a novice as about a third. Sigurd the Tamer, bow in hand and some twenty points of Archery, read about 1500 "of strength" and set out alone after grizzly bears (1554) three times in half an hour; the hunt's `Daring` and the flight's `Bearable` ask this number.
- *Decision (`BotWill.Settle(echo)`, `EchoDeaths`):* work that had been put down and dies with its bot is settled died with its trade, counted apart, and not in the headline: one death, one died ending.
- *Decision (`BotWalk.Thrashing`, `ThrashPlans` 30, `ThrashMs` 20 s, `Thrashed`):* more than thirty plans at one fixed goal in twenty seconds ends the walk. Odile stepped between (1448, 3907) and (1449, 3907) and planned 601 roads in forty seconds; each crow-fly step "closer" reset the no-progress count, and neither `MaxPlansWithoutCloser` nor `MaxEmptyPlans` ever fired. A chase and a company's places are not asked.
- *Watch:* "into a dungeon" in `gates route`; hunts by novices and "was winning"; the Resolve headline's died against "more pieces of work that had been put down died with their bot"; "walks ended for planning one place"; the dashboard's fixed-goal share.

**29.09.2026 · build 329 (written by an Opus agent, merged by Opus) · Guilds settle in empty town buildings; Britain costs 10,000**
- *Why (Patrick's idea of 29.09.2026, evening: "1–2 guilds may settle in different towns, but there must be an empty and suitable building for it; when a guild settles there, a door is put in and a sign hung on the wall. There may be guilds in Britain, but settling there costs 10,000g; that counts as the guild's home. They still have to raise a hall and take influence"):* a guild's seat was a bare point — by hand, in the file, where its hall stood, or since the morning a random spot within forty tiles of another town's middle (`BotSeat.Choose`: "The Anchor at 1401,3833, The Wolf at 2512,518, The Needle at 2248,1204"). Nothing on the map showed it and nothing in a town belonged to anybody.
- *Found on the way:* this world was decorated with `[Decorate` alone — the save holds 27 `DarkWoodDoor`s and no `Sign` at all (read off `Saves/Items/Items.idx`), so `[DoorGen` and `[SignGen` were never run. Almost every town building has a doorway with no door in it; "without a door" is the rule, and "empty" is what has to be told.
- *Decision (`BotHouseSurvey`, new folder `BotGuildHouse/`):* the towns' boxes (`BotTowns`) are read for doorways exactly as the engine's door generator reads them (`DoorGenerator.IsWestFrame`/`IsEastFrame` two or three tiles along a row, `IsNorthFrame`/`IsSouthFrame` down a column, the door at the frames' height), with a floor on the door tiles by land and statics. Both sides of each doorway are flooded with the planner's step model (`BotStep.Mask`, four ways, one storey: 6 below to 12 above the doorway, every doorway shut, cells keyed by tile and storey); a side past `MaxArea` (400) is the street, a side that stops is a room; rooms on both sides of a doorway are one building. Kept: a floor of `MinArea` (64) to 400, `RoofShare` (0.75) under a roof or upper storey, at most `MostEntrances` (2) ways out, no forge, anvil or hearth in the statics. The heart (the seat) is the floor tile nearest the middle on the door's storey. Sliced at `SliceMs` (6) a tick and cached in `Data/bot-guild-houses.bin` by the map files' fingerprint and the four numbers; never under `Saves`.
- *Why 64:* the 7 × 7 cottages (42–49 tiles of floor) are 40 of Britain's 97 buildings with a way out, 46 of Nujel'm's 63 — private homes by the world's design. Eight by eight is the first size past them; the kept buildings are the two-room houses and halls of 64–400 tiles.
- *Decision (live checks, `BotHouseSurvey.Occupied`, every boot, every ten minutes and before every settling):* not free when any floor tile lies in a region other than the town's own (the inns are unnamed `NoLogoutDelay` town regions — Vesper's inn at 2952,864 was the building the offline pass kept that should not have been); a spawner on or beside the floor, or a creature whose home is on it (a shop, a bank, a healer, an inn); a door already in a doorway (unless the guild's own); a house over it; a forge, anvil or hearth set down as an item; its street not joined to home by the gates.
- *Decision (`BotGuildHouses`, the settler, once a `LookMs` (60 s)):* each guild wishes once, kept across restarts — abroad by `BotSeat.AbroadShare` (0.5, the morning's order), or Britain; a guild at a bare seat by another town wishes abroad. **Abroad:** the free building nearest the bank of the fit town (gates join it to home, `BotSettle` says a road, a bank, shops — `FitTownsOnly`) with the fewest guild houses, its own town first, at most `MostPerTown` (2), for `TownPrice` (0 — the order names Britain's price only). A guild seated at a bare point moves into a building (`Rehouse`): in its own town when one is free, else — while it has no hall — in another fit town; with a hall it moves only within its own town, since anywhere else would carry the hall across the island. **Britain:** the guild raises its hall first (`BritainAfterHall`), then, when `BotEstate.Fund` holds `BritainPrice` (10,000), it is levied like a hall (chest first, then members) and paid into the city's treasury (`BotCity.Tax`, as a claim's price is), at most `MostInBritain` (3), the free building nearest its hall. A guild that raised its hall at home while it waited for a building abroad turns to Britain.
- *Decision (what "seated in Britain" means in the code):* a house in a Britain building, bought — not a point. Its heart is the seat; `BotRelocate.Forced` returns Britain for its members, so they live there even if they had chosen another town, as members of a guild housed abroad live abroad; they are born and rise in the building. A guild with no house is not seated in Britain: it lives where it did (the population's home, its hall looked for from there), which is the free default Patrick's price is set against. A building is required in Britain too because the price should buy the same thing a town house is — a door, a sign, a home — and Britain has 20 free ones.
- *Decision (settling):* instant, at the guild's level, as `BotSeat.Choose` was: the engine's `CanFit` on every door tile (as `DoorGenerator.AddDoor` asks), the price levied if any, then a `BotGuildDoor` in every doorway — the dark wooden door with the generator's facings (a row: WestCW, or WestCW + EastCCW linked; a column: SouthCW, or NorthCCW + SouthCW) — and a `BotGuildSign` beside the first (a west-facing sign one west and one out for a door in a row, north-facing one out and one north for a column: the commonest place of the 41 Britain shop signs within three tiles of a doorway in `signs.cfg`, every one on the outside), wooden abroad, brass in Britain, named "Guild [TAG]". The members follow at `BotRelocate`'s next look ("… lives in Minoc from now on: The Wolf is seated there").
- *Decision (the door):* unlocked in the engine's terms, refusing at the handle: `BotGuildDoor.Use` opens for a member, staff, anybody inside, and anybody once the guild holds no house there; everybody else is told "That is locked" (the engine's 502503) and counted. Locked would be a wall to the planner for members too (`BotStep.BlockedByItems`), and keys die with packs (`BotEstate.Unlock`).
- *Decision (hooks, all small and commented):* `BotSeat.Of` answers the house's heart before any other seat; `BotSeat.Home` answers it before the hall (born, risen, walked home to inside a guarded town); `BotSeat.Moving` still carries a housed guild's hall towards the seat the hall itself last set, or an exile's move would be undone by the next carry; `BotSeat.Choose` no longer picks a bare point while houses run (the name's wish is redrawn); a seat set by hand (`do seat`) pins the guild — it leaves its house and is not settled again until a reset or a new founding; `BotResidence.Span` puts a body within `Spread` (3) of a heart, not the population's ten; `BotGuilds.Worth` counts a house; Argus's `reset` empties every house (`BotGuildHouses.Wipe`).
- *Decision (persistence):* `BotGuildHouseStore` ("BotGuildHouses", shape 1) keeps each guild's building by the tile of its first door, its heart, town, price and date, each guild's wish and the pinned guilds. The doors and signs are world items and the world save keeps them. At every boot every house is found in the survey again, its doors and sign put back if the world lost them, and a door or sign of ours standing in any surveyed doorway nobody holds is taken down. A guild gone from the roll for `GoneLooks` (2) looks leaves its house: door and sign come down.
- *Also:* the `Houses:` summary line after `Treasuries:`; per guild on the page `hall` (now the real hall — it carried the seat until now), `seat`, `house`, `fund`, `goal`, `saving`; per town `houses` and `free`; the map draws the hall in the fields, the house in the town (a square in the guild's colour with a door), a bare seat as a ring; the guild card and tooltip say house, hall, squares and money against the goal. `"house"` events on the stream. Module `GuildHouse` (`bots.guildhouse.enabled`), config `Configuration/bot-guildhouse.json` (starter written empty), registered after Estate, Travel, Residence; `regen-map.py` knows the folder.
- *Measured (engine, scratch test host — the real Felucca files, `regions.json`, the world decorated from `Data/Decoration` and a spawner laid at every spawn-file location; not the shard):* 287 buildings kept, surveyed in 1.7–1.8 s of loop over ~210 slices (worst 29 ms with a cold step cache; 150 ms and worst 6 ms warm; read back from the file in no time, identical). Free after the live checks: Britain 20, Minoc 2, Trinsic 9, Vesper 4, Yew 19, Cove 0 (and Jhelom 21, Nujel'm 8, Ocllo 3, Moonglow 3, Skara Brae 1, Bucs 1, which no road reaches). Not free: 127 with a spawner, 30 with a hearth or forge item, 18 with a door, 23 in an inn's rooms. A settling into Minoc's 273-tile building at 2426,527 put a linked pair (0x6A5 / 0x6A7) into 2425–2426,535 and a sign (0xBD0, "west") at 2424,536; the door refused a stranger ("turned away 1") and opened for the guild's leader; a second guild read the building as taken; the wipe left nothing standing and the building free again.
- *Watch:*
  - boot: `Guild houses are on: a guild settles in an empty town building — a floor of 64 to 400 tiles, 75 % of it roofed, at most 2 ways in — 2 to a town fit to live in, for nothing; in Britain 3 at most, for 10000gp paid to the city once its hall stands; …`;
  - first boot: `Guild houses: the towns were surveyed from the map in …ms … — Cove 2 of 10, Britain 56 of 97, …`; later boots `… from Data/bot-guild-houses.bin …`; then `Guild houses: N read back from the save (…); N doors and signs put back …, N of nobody's taken down`;
  - within a minute or two of the survey: `The Lantern will settle in an empty building of another town` / `… in Britain, for 10000gp once its hall stands` / `The Wolf will settle in an empty building by its seat at 2512,518, or in another town with room`, then `The Wolf settles in Minoc: the empty building at 2426,527 (273 tiles of floor, 1 way in) is its house now — a door put into the doorway at 2425,535 and its sign hung beside it; nothing paid, the building stood empty; its 6 members live in Minoc from now on, born and risen there`, then the residence lines `… lives in Minoc from now on: The Wolf is seated there`;
  - `Seats: … The Wolf at 2426,527 (its house in Minoc) …`; `Houses: The Wolf in Minoc at 2426,527, …; waiting: …; 287 buildings surveyed, free now: Britain 20, Minoc 1, …; … N strangers turned away at a guild's door`;
  - the hall plots: `the steward … found nothing to build on N times` for guilds housed in Minoc (mountains) or Yew (woods) — the search starts at the house now;
  - the page: houses drawn in town, halls in the fields; hover says which.
- *Undo:* `Running: false` in `bot-guildhouse.json` (or `bots.guildhouse.enabled`): no seat answers from a house, the settler stops, the doors stay and open for anybody (a door of nobody's house bars nobody). `do reset` takes every door and sign down. `Rehouse: false` leaves the three bare seats where they are.

**29.09.2026 · build (next) (written by an Opus agent) · A guild's money is a store: dues into the chest, the chest counted, the chest's share of a short levy handed back**
- *Seen (every Estate line of 29.09.2026, the day of the wipe):* "no halls stand; … 0gp levied off 0 members …; The Lantern has 0 of 5000 and is 5000 short, … (every guild 0 of 5000); the steward offered a hall 0 times, held off 0 times …, found nothing to build on 0 times"; the staker "looked 1366 times: … 1366 guilds had no hall to want ground near"; `Guilds: … 77gp stood for members 2 times, 3201 times a guild could not`.
- *Root cause, measured before anything was changed (C2, C8):* a guild's money was never a store. `BotEstate.Fund` was the sum, at the moment of asking, of each member's wealth above `Keep` (300), and it did not count the chest. The middling purse read 19–242gp in all 207 money lines of the day (68gp at the median); and whoever rose above 300 was stripped back to it within minutes by `BotGuilds.Stand`, which draws on the same spare, richest first, to pay other members' armour and — since build 259 — their compulsory supplies (and on a stand that falls short hands the part raised to the asker). 53 of the 207 money lines name a fattest purse of exactly 300gp; the session of 14:49–16:08 stood 29,374gp for members. Two claimants on one pool, and the one that spends every minute wins against the one that must wait for five thousand. The one thing that does keep, the chest, is fed only by tithes on held ground; held ground is a hall's yard or a claim, and a claim is offered only to a guild with a hall: a ring of three gates. Four callers (enlarge, outpost, widen twice) had learnt to add the chest to `Fund` by hand; the steward, fitter, hirer, supplier and staker never saw it.
- *Instrument first (`BotDues.Describe`, the `Treasuries:` line after `Estate:`):* per guild, the chest and the members' spare separately, how many members stand above the keep and how rich the richest is, what dues brought in and what the chest kept back, and the guild's seat, hall and squares; globally what members stood for each other. With `Dues 0` it still shows the cause: "chest 0gp + members' spare 0gp (0 of 10 above the 300gp keep, the richest 212gp)".
- *Decision (`BotDues`, `BotEstate/BotDues.cs`):* `Dues` (0.2) of the coin a member's settled work brought in (the takings' own `Coin`) is paid into its guild's chest in `BotWill.Settle`, right after the tithe and less whatever the tithe just paid into the same chest, pack first then account; booked aside for the member (`BotYield.Aside`), so a put-down errand does not read it as its own loss; not for The Shadow; nothing at or above `DuesCeiling` (20,000). Coin moves from a member to its guild; nothing is minted.
- *Decision (`BotEstate.Fund` = chest + `BotEstate.Spare`):* the chest counts wherever the guild's means are asked; the four hand-made additions are removed. `BotEstate.Spare` (the members' half) is what the crown's tax is reckoned on (`BotRevel.Tax`), and `Take` no longer draws the chest for the tax: six per cent of a chest every quarter of an hour would be a fifth of a guild's savings an hour.
- *Decision (`BotDues.Goal`, `DuesSaving`):* while a guild has no hall the chest keeps the hall's price back from the everyday draws — `BotProvision.Fund` (supplies) and a ship's price (`BotSea`) draw only what it holds above that — and after the hall, the price of a house in Britain while it saves for one. Supplies still come from the members' spare through `BotGuilds.Stand`, as before; the estate's own levies (hall, bench, merchant, claims, enlarging) draw the whole chest.
- *Decision (`BotEstate.Take`, `BotChest.Return`):* a levy that falls short puts the chest's share back. Every caller treats a short levy as no purchase and refunds the members only; until now the chest's share was simply gone — with a chest holding most of a hall's price, a steward who reached the plot after the members had spent their part would have thrown a guild's day of saving away.
- *Expected, not measured:* settled work brought in 14,176gp/h (17:38–18:38) and 17,569gp/h (19:12–19:36) in positive coin, nine tenths of it to guild members; a fifth is 2,500–3,100gp/h into seven chests: a guild of fifteen to 5,000 in nine to eleven hours, a guild of six in about a day. Then the steward (it starts looking at half the price), the hall, and the first four claims, which cost nothing.
- *Watch:* boot `Estate ready: … levied off its chest and then its members …; members pay 20 % of what their work brings in into their guild's chest, up to 20000gp a chest, and a chest keeps the price of the hall (or of a house in Britain) back from everyday draws`; every 5 minutes `Treasuries: dues of 20 % …: Ngp paid in N times …; The Crown: chest Ngp + members' spare 0gp (…) = N of the hall's 5000gp, dues Ngp in, Ngp kept back; no seat, no hall, 0 squares; …` — the rate is the difference between two lines; the Estate line's "has N of 5000" now includes the chest; then `the steward offered a hall N times`, `took on hall`, `raised the hall of …`, and the staker's `N claims made, N won`; `Money:` "taken out of bots … by decisions outside their work" grows by the dues; `supplies: … the guild paid N restocks` may fall while chests save (their shortfall now goes to `Stand`), and deaths a minute should be read against it; the chest's `(Ngp handed back from levies that fell short)`.
- *Undo:* `dial BotDues.Share 0` (or `Dues: 0` in `bot-estate.json`) stops the dues; `DuesSaving: false` lets supplies draw the whole chest again. The chest counted in `Fund`, the tax on members only and the returned share are repairs and have no dial.

---

**Open (§6), for Patrick:**
1. *The rate.* A fifth of the coin gets a big guild its hall in nine to eleven hours on the day's income, a small one in a day. Faster is `dial BotDues.Share 0.35` (about five and a half hours) or a lower `BotEstate.Price`; the `Treasuries:` line gives the rate to judge by. Which lever, if any?
2. *The three bare seats.* With `Rehouse` on, The Wolf moves into a Minoc building, and The Anchor (Jhelom: no road in the book) and The Needle (Cove: no bank, and no free building of 64 tiles) move to a free building in the nearest fit town with room — Yew, then Minoc, Trinsic, Vesper by distance from home. Keep that, or leave bare seats alone (`Rehouse: false`)?
3. *Island towns.* Jhelom has 21 free buildings, Nujel'm 8, Moonglow 3 — but "reachable on foot" and `FitTownsOnly` keep them out. Should a town reached by ship (BotSea, build 321) or moongate be settled in?
4. *Britain before the hall?* `BritainAfterHall` makes a Britain-wishing guild raise its hall first. Or should the home be bought first?
5. *A guild that finds nothing abroad* waits (said once an hour). Should it turn to Britain after some hours?
6. *Door strength.* The door refuses strangers at the handle but not the twenty seconds it stands open after a member. A truly locked door would need the planner to know who is asking. Enough as it is?
7. *Two guilds in one town* live within a few dozen tiles; their halls will be looked for from neighbouring seats and may border, which sours them (`BotRegard`). Accept as the risk of expansion, or keep one guild a town (`MostPerTown 1`)?
8. *The hall abroad.* A housed guild's hall is looked for from its town house: round Minoc (mountains) and Yew (forest) the plot search may find little; the steward's "found nothing to build on" will say so.

---

*How the survey was checked (scratch, not in the patch):* `UOContent.Tests` in a copy of the patched tree, referencing BotAIv2, with the client files (`MODERNUO_TEST_DATA_DIR`), `regions.json`, `[Decorate` from `Data/Decoration/{Britannia,Felucca}` and a `Spawner` at each Felucca spawn-file location; `BotTowns.Ensure`, `BotHouseSurvey.Step` to ready, `Occupied` for every building, a settling into Minoc by reflection, the door used by a stranger and a member, `Wipe`, and the cache written and read back. What that host has not: vendors standing (spawners do not spawn there), the gates (the reach check is skipped), live guilds, the residence module, a save and a restart.

**29.09.2026 · build 325 (written by an Opus agent, merged by Opus) · The berth has to take the hull a deed puts down**
- *What 322 wrote (session 19-58):* "Rhiannel failed at voyage: waiting at Vesper for the berth: 0 in 13.4 min — could not put to sea from Vesper: the berth at Vesper is taken". The 13.4 minutes were about eleven of walking from where she was pressed and the two-minute `BerthWaitMs`. No ship had been in the water on 321 or 322: no "put to sea" line, and no "ships with a bot's name on them … at boot".
- *Cause:* a deed or a dry-docked ship always puts down a *new* ship, and a new ship faces north. `BaseBoatDeed.OnPlacement` asks `CanFit` of the new ship's own item id. `BotDocks.Try` chose each berth for the hull lying the way the harbour lies. For an east–west dock it never asked whether the north hull fits there too. `BotHelm.Embark` did ask it (`FitsNow(north)`), and when that failed it reported "is taken" and waited for a berth that could never take the ship.
  - Vesper's berth (3010, 748): the north hull's own tiles (multi 0x0) cover (3010, 752) and (3010, 753), which are the shore.
  - Buccaneer's Den (2743, 2160): the north hull covers seven shore tiles.
  - The three other east–west docks (Trinsic, Nujel'm, Magincia) take the north hull by chance.
- *Measured offline (client map0 + statics0, the multi's 36 hull tiles, the 13 berths from the 19:58 boot):*
  - **2 of 13 docks were refused on every departure:** Vesper and Buccaneer's Den. Arrivals there were unaffected, because landing puts no ship down.
  - **The other 11 fit:** their berths take the north hull.
  - **No decoration item stands in any berth's rectangle:** 26,107 items were checked from `Data/Decoration/Britannia` and `Felucca`.
  - **With the new rule the same shores give** Vesper (3012, 748) and Buccaneer's Den (2742, 2157), both still east–west with the plank 3 and 4 tiles from the shore. The other eleven berths are unchanged.
- *Decision (`BotDocks.Try`, `BotSeaWindow.Places`, `BotSeaChart.TilesNorth`):* a berth candidate must float the north hull's own tiles (read from `MultiData`) and the rectangle of its lie. The best `Candidates` (8) are then asked of the live world (`BotSeaChart.Occupant`). One with something on it other than a ship — decoration is items, a building is a multi, and the map files show neither — is passed over (`BotDocks.Occupied`) with a line naming it.
- *Decision (instrument, `BotSeaChart.Occupant`, `BotBerthBlock`):* the engine's two `CanFit` loops, in the engine's order, answer in words what keeps a ship off a berth, by kind:
  - `Ground` — a hull tile that is not water at sea level;
  - `Static` — a static of the map;
  - `Ship` — another ship's hull, tillerman, hold or plank, named by its owner and whether it is at anchor;
  - `Multi` — any other multi;
  - `Item`.

  The refusal reads "the berth at Vesper (x, y) is taken: dry ground at (3010, 752): land 0x… at Z …". It is counted in `BotHelm.TakenByShip/Ground/Static/Multi/Item` (once per voyage per berth; a voyage waiting asks every beat), which the `Sea:` summary prints even before any ship has sailed. At boot every berth is asked once: "{Town}'s berth N at (x, y) cannot be put into now: …".
- *Decision (only a ship is waited for, `BotVoyage.Refused`):* when a berth is taken, the voyage first walks to another berth of the same dock that is free now ("{Name} goes to {Dock}'s berth N at (x, y): …", `BotVoyage.Shifted`). Failing that, a ship in the berth is waited for up to `BerthWaitMs`, and every berth is asked again each beat (`Waited`). Anything else ends the voyage at once, naming what was there. The old wait was granted to any refusal worded "taken".
- *Decision (more berths per dock, `BotDocks.MostBerths` 3, `BerthReach` 48):* after its first berth, a dock keeps up to two more from the next shores along the coast within 48 tiles. Each has its own harbour.
  - Where that harbour reaches the open sea in a different cell, the way between the two cells is drawn with the lanes (`BotBerth.Link`, the same sliced A*). A berth with no such way is dropped.
  - A voyage from another berth sails its own harbour, then the link, then the lane (`BotSeaLane.Course(from, berth, …)`), lying as that berth lies.
  - The boot line reads "Sea: N berths at 13 docks, M besides the first (… dropped for want of a way …, … passed over for something in the world on them)".
- *Decision (the harbour clears the population's own litter, `BotHelm.Clear`):* an idle ship in a berth — one with a bot's name on it and no voyage sailing it — is cleared the way the boot recovers such ships. Bots and beasts aboard are put on the berth's shore, then the ship is dry-docked into its owner's pack, or scuttled when the owner is gone. Such a ship is one left at anchor after a refused dry-docking, a death aboard, or a boarding that could not dock the ship back. Otherwise it would hold the berth for the engine's nine days of decay. Players' ships are never touched. Counted in `BotHelm.Cleared`.
- *Also:* the `Sea:` line's helm clause no longer reads "no ship has put to sea" when berths have been refused.
- *Watch:*
  - **Boot:** "Sea: Vesper has a dock: … the ship put down at (3012, 748) lying east–west"; "Sea: Buccaneer's Den has a dock: … (2742, 2157)"; "has another berth"; "Sea: N berths at 13 docks"; any "cannot be put into now:" warning; any "is passed over:".
  - **Play:** `dial BotSea.Grant true`, then `dial BotSea.Order Rhiannel to Nujel'm`, then Grant back to false. Expect "has put to sea from Vesper for Nujel'm". Also watch for "goes to {Dock}'s berth", "waiting at … for the berth: {occupant}", and the summary's "berths found taken by a ship N times, by ground N …". `TakenByGround` should stay at nought: a nonzero count means the berth search and the engine disagree.
- *Status:* **attempt**. The patch is `boats2.patch`: five files of BotSea only, with no hook in shared files. It builds with 0 errors on the 321 snapshot with the 322 BotSea overlaid. Not run on a shard.

**29.09.2026 · build 324 (written by Opus) · The early flight; a thousand shopkeepers**
- *Measured on 323 (20:16–20:26, 10 min):* 522 of 584 endings finished (89 %, from 85 % on 322), 28 failed, 7 dropped, 27 died (from 35). Mine 92 % (72 %), homeward 100 % (62 %), hunt 90 % (69 %); two walkers stepped through a teleporter that had not fired for them; one member left on a march (three per march on 322). Rescue 32 % finished, 18 % dropped; flee 47 %.

**29.09.2026 · build 321 (written by an Opus agent, merged by Opus) · Ships: the bots sail to the towns no road reaches**
- *Why (Patrick's point 7 of 29.09.2026, "teach the bots to travel by sea, on boats"):* the boot line reads "Towns: 10 of 18 can be walked to from home: Cove, Britain, Minoc, Trinsic, Vesper, Yew, Serpent's Hold, Buccaneer's Den, Delucia, Papua". Jhelom, Moonglow, Magincia, Nujel'm, Ocllo and Skara Brae are across water (Wind and the Heartwood are beyond the sea, in the dungeon block). A ship is the engine's own way over it, and it moves only where `BaseBoat.CanFit` lets it: every hull tile water at the ship's own Z, nothing else at or above it. A bot cannot steer by the tillerman — his commands are speech keywords the client encodes, and a bot's `Say` carries none — so the helm calls what those keywords call.
- *Measured before writing (a Python pass over the client's map0/statics0 with the engine's own rules, 29.09.2026):* 14,512,366 water land tiles at Z −5 (the next height has 1,118); the small ship (multi 0x0) is 5 × 11 and reaches 5 from its middle; with that reach 217,920 of 327,680 cells of eight are open and 214,506 of them are one body, the open sea; 13 of the 14 charted towns get a dock (Minoc's bay is too narrow within 128 tiles — Minoc is walked to), harbours 4–39 tiles; all 78 pairs of docks are joined by the open sea (Britain–Moonglow 3,814 tiles, –Jhelom 3,405, –Magincia 2,651, –Ocllo 2,805, –Skara Brae 5,568 round the south, Yew–Skara Brae 1,653); the worst course expands 266,138 cells, all 78 together 4.6 million.
- *Decision (`BotSea/BotSeaChart`):* the water charted once from the map through the engine's tile API, sliced at `SliceMs` (6 ms) a tick: a 64-bit mask of floatable tiles per map block (the engine's rule; statics read only for blocks with water land, so the chart does not pull every forest's statics into memory), a cell = one block, open when the cell and `Half` (5, read from `MultiData`) tiles round it float — a ship whose middle is anywhere in an open cell fits there facing any way and can turn there; diagonals only past two open corners; three cells shut along the engine's wrap rectangle. Bodies of open water are labelled and the largest is the open sea. Kept in `Data/bot-sea-chart.bin` keyed by `TileMatrix.MapFilesFingerprint`, so only the first boot after a map change pays the read (about a second of loop in ~170 slices, and the engine's tile cache then holds the land of the whole map, ~70 MB, until restart); later boots read ~0.5 MB.
- *Decision (`BotSea/BotDocks`):* a dock per town, found, not written: from the square (or `Docks` pin in `bot-sea.json`) ring by ring to `Reach` (200) the first standable ground beside floatable water joined to the square (`BotGates.Joined`) is a shore; the berth is where the ship's hull fits lying north–south or east–west with a plank within `Gangway` (6, the engine plank's own reach) of the shore; the harbour is a breadth-first search over hull-fitting tiles (statics everywhere, canals included) within `HarbourReach` (128) to the first open cell of the open sea, kept as its turns. A shore whose harbour is a pond is passed over with every shore within `Spread` (16) of it, up to `Tries` (24).
- *Decision (`BotSea/BotSeaLanes`, `BotSeaCourse`):* one lane per pair of docks no road joins, A* over open cells (octile, stamped marks, resumable heap, sliced by the same deadline), kept as the cells where the heading turns. A town not `FromHome` whose dock has a lane to a dock home walks to is `BotTowns.Town.BySea`.
- *Decision (`BotSea/BotHelm`):* the ship steered every `StrokeMs` (750, the engine's pre-High-Seas interval) by `BaseBoat.Move` at `Speed` 3 ahead or ahead-diagonal and 1 sideways/back (the engine's own speeds), turning with `BaseBoat.Turn` in the open sea and only end-for-end in a harbour. Embarking: the deed's (or docked ship's) own `OnPlacement` at the berth, `Key.UseOn` to unlock the plank, `Plank.Open`, the plank's own boarding line (`Z + 3`), captain and beasts (and a company, if handed one) onto deck places, plank closed and locked, anchor raised, `Journey.Finish`. Landing: anchor, the dock's shore (or the nearest joined ground within `LandReach`), crew ashore, `CheckDryDock`/`EndDryDock` from the shore — the docked ship goes back in the pack. Blocked: a step to either side, then after `StuckStrokes` (8) land if within reach of the far berth, put back if still in the home harbour, otherwise shut the cell ahead (`ShutMs` 10 min) and ask a new course, up to `MostReroutes` (3). A captain who dies aboard leaves the ship at anchor (counted); one no longer aboard likewise; no headway for `BecalmedMs` (3 min) or past twice the course's time plus `SlackMs` is a wreck: captain and crew carried to the nearest dock and the ship dry-docked from there — the only hand-move in the module, counted and said. The helm resets the captain's (and crew's) `Refusals` every stroke, so `BotPopulation.Rescue` never carries a bot home out of the middle of the sea. At boot, ships with a bot's name on them and no voyage are recovered (aboard carried ashore, ship dry-docked into the owner's pack) or scuttled when the owner is gone (`BaseBoat.Boats`, not the world).
- *Decision (`BotSea/BotVoyage`, `BotSea.Travel`, `BotSeafarer`):* the voyage is a deed — buy (nearest shopkeeper selling `SmallBoatDeed`: shipwrights and provisioners, 10,177 gp; the guild stands the rest by `BotProvision.Fund` when `GuildPays`; the price booked aside, the ship kept in the bond's item list so nothing sells it and not on its issue list so a lost ship is not re-issued on resurrection), walk to the dock, embark, then only watch the helm; after landing a walk into the town (`Arrival` 10) or home. Steadfast, resumes, committed and `Still` at sea (the helm's clocks, not the labour clock). `Where` is the departure dock until aboard and the goal after — the appraisal vetoes work on ground no gate joins to the bot. Prior 8 (the journey's); the way home `HomeWorth` 6 and unpaid, like the walk home. `BotSea.Travel` is asked by the traveller first: a bot on home's land by `Share` (0.25), a bot on an island always (it travels by sea or not at all); towns weighted by curiosity over the lane's sailings; the departure dock is the one that makes walk + voyage shortest (`BotSea.Plan`), so Britain→Skara Brae sets out from Yew; offered only if the bot has a ship or its purse plus what its guild could stand covers one (`CanSail`). `BotSeafarer` offers the way home to a bot on land not joined to its seat, once barren for `BotHomeward.BarrenFor`.
- *Hooks in shared files (four, each commented):* `BotCore.Configure` registers `BotSeaModule` after travel; `BotBeat.Summarise` prints `Sea: …`; `BotTowns.Town.BySea`, read by `BotTowns.Within` (a sea town's ground is the population's to work) and `BotTowns.Describe`; `BotTraveller.Propose` asks `BotSea.Travel` before the road loop.
- *Dials (`Configuration/bot-sea.json`, PascalCase):* `Running`, `Share` 0.25, `Furthest` 8000, `Prior` 8, `HomeWorth` 6, `GuildPays` true, `Grant` false, `Cache` true, `DockReach` 200, `Docks` {"Town": [x, y]}. Live through the door: `BotHelm.StrokeMs/Speed/StuckStrokes/BecalmedMs/MostReroutes/SlackMs`, `BotDocks.Gangway/HarbourReach/Tries/Spread`, `BotSeaChart.SeaLevel/SliceMs`, `BotSeaCourse.ShutMs`, `BotVoyage.BerthWaitMs/AshoreMs`, and `BotSea.Order` — `dial BotSea.Order <bot> to <town>` presses that bot to sail now (`BotWill.Press`); with `dial BotSea.Grant true` it is handed a ship instead of buying one (trials only: a world wiped this morning has a middling purse of 66 gp).
- *Watch:* boot — "Sea is on: a traveller on home's land is offered a town across the sea 25 % of the time", "Sea: charted the water of Felucca from the map: N tiles float a ship, N of 327680 cells of eight are open … the open sea N cells" (second boot: "from Data/bot-sea-chart.bin"), "Sea: {Town} has a dock: ashore at (x, y, z), the ship put down at (x, y) lying …", "Sea: N of 18 towns have a dock", "Sea: N lanes drawn between N docks, N pairs joined by road and left to it, N with no way by sea; the longest …", "Towns: N more can be sailed to from home: …"; in play — "bought a ship from … for 10177gp", "has put to sea from {From} for {To}: N tiles in N legs", "has sailed from {From} to {To} in N minutes and stepped ashore at (x, y); the ship is dry-docked in its pack", "is in {Town} after N minutes, by sea from …", "died aboard off", "was wrecked on the way", "put back into", "sails on by a new course"; the five-minute "Sea: N voyages begun, N arrived, N lost; N ships bought for Ngp …" (Moves against Blocks, SideSteps, Reroutes, Wrecked should stay near nought); "Travel: … Moonglow (by sea, N arrivals …)". Expect few voyages until a guild can stand 10,177 gp; to see one at once: `dial BotSea.Grant true`, `dial BotSea.Order <name> to Moonglow`.
- *Not done:* a company is carried only through the `company` argument of `BotVoyage`/`BotHelm.Embark` — no delve or sweep leader calls it yet, and a member's squad stations on a moving deck are untested; ships are not drawn on the dashboard; the chart ignores the second wrap rectangle (the lost lands' water: Delucia and Papua are walked to); a ship lost with a dead captain stays at anchor until the engine's nine-day decay; `regen-map.py` does not list the `BotSea` folder yet. Nothing here has run on the shard: the chart, docks and lanes were checked only by the Python pass above.
- *Status:* **attempt**.
