**29.09.2026 · build 320 (written by an Opus agent, merged by Opus) · Roads are remembered, and only a cheaper one replaces them**
- *Why (Patrick's point 3 of the evening: "Paths 99 %. Paths and graphs must be remembered; they can only be optimised"):* the tiered navigation planned every request afresh. The summary of 18:53 read 2244 routes asked in 14 407 ms over fifteen minutes — 6.4 ms a route since the danger hook (build 297 measured 4–7 ms against 0.7 before it), 23 239 938 medium nodes expanded, 139 457 877 danger lookups — for a population that walks the same few dozen roads (halls, banks, mouths, the shops of the north) again and again, and re-draws the same road every time it strays or its target drifts. The roadbook re-drew every road between the towns at every boot and never learned from the walks. And the walker burned the whole ceiling on the very same search from the very same tile: "closing up on Mirthal, company 20 160" (sixty milliseconds each), 263 of 386 partials "ended no nearer than they started".
- *Decision (engine, `NavRouteMemory`, new, `Engines/Pathing/Tiered`):* every node of a planned route is a place to join it, keyed by where the node stands and the goal's cluster. `NavigationService.Route` asks the memory first (`Recall`): the start's cluster flood picks the cheapest node it reaches that begins a remembered road to the goal's cluster, the goal's flood the cheapest node of the road's last run it is reached from, and the road from there is handed out exactly as the planner hands one out (one point a cluster, a gate's near side left out). A walker on the road — strayed, re-drawn, the second bot out of the same yard — gets the suffix (`Middles`). Ends fewer than `NearClusters` (3) clusters apart are left to the planner.
- *Decision (only cheaper replaces, `Offer`):* a newly planned route takes a place from the road held there only when what is left of it from that node to the same goal costs less (ground cost, `NavCost` units, compared at the moment of the offer against the same ends); never a dearer one (`Kept`). A road all of whose places were taken is dropped (`Superseded`). Bounded by `Capacity` (2048 roads) and `NodeCapacity` (262 144 nodes, ≈ 12–14 MB), the least lately used first (`Evicted`).
- *Decision (the ground changes, `Prove`):* each run of a road's nodes in one cluster keeps the cluster's version (`NavGraph.ClusterVersion`) and an order- and id-independent signature of its nodes and edges (`NavRouteMemory.Sign`). Same version: valid. New version, same signature (every cluster after a boot, the clusters beside a house redrawn at boot): the node ids are looked up again by position, the stamp renewed (`Rejoined`), the road stands. New signature: forgotten (`Invalidated`) and planned afresh. A cluster being drawn right now: not served, not forgotten (`Waiting`). `GroundChanged` (a house raised or taken down) also forgets every road within a cluster of the rectangle, for the shortcut a demolished house can open beside a road that crosses nothing that changed; `Shun` forgets every road through the gate a walker could not pass. A road planned while any gate is shunned (`HierarchicalPlanner.Shunning`) expires with the shun (`ShunMs`, 10 min; `Expired`) and is never written to disk — a way round a shunned gate kept for good would be served for ever.
- *Decision (the danger, `NavigationService.Planned`):* the memory keeps **ground** roads: a road not remembered is planned with the danger hook off (`GroundPlans`), offered, and then read against the hook: quiet all along, it is walked as it is — it is the road the danger-aware planner would find, since every road costs at least its ground price and none is cheaper on the ground — one plan as before, but the cheaper kind (940 nodes against 2500–4400). Bloodied, it is planned again with the hook on (`RoundPlans`) and that way round is kept as a detour for the pair of clusters (`OfferDetour`, `DetourMs` 5 min = `BotQuad.SightMs`, `DetourCapacity` 512), served while it is no bloodier than when drawn and the ground road no less bloody — the reason to go round still stands — and dropped otherwise (`DetoursDropped`). A remembered road that crosses blood now (`Bloodied`) goes straight to the second plan. When the planners find no way round within budget, the ground road is walked rather than the old chart (`RoundFallbacks`).
- *Decision (kept across restarts, `NavRouteFile`, new):* `Data/Pathfinding/navroutes-{map}.nvr` beside the graph's file, map-fingerprinted as the graph's; written every `RouteWriteEveryMs` (10 min) when changed, by a worker, from arrays that never change once a road is made, never while the world saves, and synchronously at shutdown; read by the graph's own boot worker and laid into the memory when the graph is in place (`Adopt`), each road proved by its signatures the first time it is asked. Config keys `pathfinding.routes.remember` (off = the planners as before), `.capacity`, `.detourMs`, `.writeEveryMs`.
- *Decision (`BotPath.MemoMs` 2000):* a short search asked again within two seconds with the very same question — same tile, target, arrival and ceiling, no exclusions, doors as doors — gets the same answer without the search. Deterministic in what it is given; what changes the question changes the key (a step, a moved target, the escalated ceiling); a starved search and a refusal are not kept; `MemoMs` 0 turns it off. Counted as `Recalled`/`RecalledMs`, not as searches.
- *Decision (`BotRoadbook.Offer`, `BotTravel.Track`):* the roads between the towns are kept in the store with their points (`BotRoadbookStore` shape 2; shape 1 still read) and only ever shortened: the boot's draw and every traveller's walk (footprints every `TrackStep` 16 tiles, the graph's own spacing; a jump over `TrackJump` 48 breaks the track) are measured the same way, square to square, and take the road's place only when shorter.
- *Decision (dashboard, `BotWebSnapshot` "routes"):* `fromMemory`, `planned`, `memoryShare` (served over served plus the plans it could have served), `memoryMs`, `plannedMs`, `savedMs`, `remembered`, `rememberedNodes`, `joinedMiddle`, `detoured`, `throughBlood`, `offeredCheaper`, `offeredNoCheaper`, `forgottenGround`, `searchesMemoized`. The page (`Data/bot-web/index.html`) does not show them yet.
- *Tests (`NavRouteMemoryTests`, 8):* the same route from its start and a suffix from along it; a cheaper route replaces and a dearer one does not; a cluster drawn again the same keeps the road and a walled gap forgets it; the file round-trips into a freshly drawn graph and a file read onto other ground is forgotten on first use; blood on the road is planned round, the way round is kept while its reason stands and dropped when the blood dries, spreads to it, or its time is up; a road round a shunned gate expires; the bound evicts the least lately used; and the price: sixty routes across the river field recalled warm in 7.0 ms against 20.2 ms planned again by the medium tier alone without the hook (0.12 against 0.34 ms each — a recall is two cluster floods and a walk along the road, the floods every plan pays too; on the shard a plan with the hook is 4–7 ms). `DangerHookTests` now runs alone (collection "Tiered navigation, one at a time"): it sets the static hook, and `StrategicPlannerTests.RiverWithAFarFord` failed at the base whenever the two ran together.
- *Expected:* the "Navigation:" line's routes cost falls from 6.4 ms each towards the served share times ~0.05 ms; `memoryShare` above one half within the first hour after a boot and near it from the first minute after a boot with the file; "the roads read the danger: N nodes asked" falls several-fold (ground plans ask nothing); journeys by purpose unchanged (≈ 99.5 %).
- *Watch:* the "Navigation:" summary every five minutes — "routes from memory: N served in Xms against M planned in Yms (K of them far enough to remember, Zms each), about Wms saved; G planned on the ground, R round the danger after, F walked on the ground for want of a way round; N roads remembered over … nodes (… places to join them) and … ways round the danger; … asked of it: … served (… joined in the middle), … round the danger, … not remembered, … through blood now, … across ground being drawn again, …; … offered: … kept new, … cheaper than what was held, … no cheaper, … declined; forgotten: … as the ground changed (… clusters drawn again the same and kept), …"; at boot "Navigation: N remembered roads of Felucca read from disk (M in the file); each is proved against the graph by its clusters' signatures the first time it is asked"; every ten minutes "Navigation: N remembered roads of Felucca written to disk in Xms"; in "Getting about:" "N asked again within 2s of the same search and answered from it (Xms of searching not done again)"; in "Travel:" "only ever shortened: N walks shorter than the road held and M not, …" and "Roads: a walk shortened {From}–{To} from {Old} steps to {New}". A rising "forgotten … as the ground changed" without houses going up is a signature that is not stable — look there first.
- *Risks:* a road joined from the far side of its start cluster costs up to a cluster's crossing more than a fresh plan (why `NearClusters` is 3); a detour can outlive a cheaper third road opening for up to `DetourMs`; the roadbook store written by this build is shape 2, which an older build refuses ("the saved roadbook is shape 2 and this build reads 1; the roads start unwalked") — a rollback loses the walk counts, not the world. Delete `navroutes-0.nvr` to start the memory empty.
- *Status:* **attempt**. *Code:* `NavRouteMemory.cs`, `NavRouteFile.cs` (new), `NavigationService.cs`, `HierarchicalPlanner.cs` (`LastPath`, `Shunning`), `BotPath.cs`, `BotRoadbook.cs`, `BotTravel.cs`, `BotWebSnapshot.cs`; tests `NavRouteMemoryTests.cs`, `DangerHookTests.cs`.

**29.09.2026 · build 320 (written by an Opus agent, merged by Opus) · Every bot lives in a town of its own**
- *Why (Patrick's order of 29.09.2026, point 5: "teach the bots to choose a town of residence, live there, hunt there, do their routine — all the same things they do in Britain; the result: the bots spread over the world"):* the population had one home. Every per-bot "home" in the code asked `BotPopulation.Where` or `BotSeat.Home`: the walk home, the flight's last resort (`BotBolt`), the herb woods, the hunting darts and the feared ground (`BotHunter`), birth and revival (`TryPlace`), the delve's rally, the release from a cell, a bot's own house, the leash. At the boot of 18:38 sixty of sixty-three bots stood in four guilds and three of the four had no seat ("The Crown has no seat, The Hammer has no seat, The Blade has no seat, The Needle at 2248,1204"), so everybody but The Needle's fifteen lived, was born and rose within 350 tiles of one tile.
- *Found on the way (18:38 boot):* `BotShops.MaxShops` (96) was full eight sweeps into the boot, every sweep round Britain ("49 … 33 … 7 … now 96"); the sweep round Cove at (2257, 1207) found "0 shopkeepers" with seven standing there. A bot living anywhere but Britain would have been sent back to Britain for every purchase.
- *Decision (`BotPopulation.HomeOf(Mobile)` → `BotResidence.Home`; `Centre` is now `HomeOf`):* the one answer to a per-bot home. In the home town (Britain, `BotSettle.HomeTown`) it is exactly what it was — the guild's hall or seat, else `Where`; in any other town it is the town's bank (`BotSettle.Hearth`), or the guild's own hall or seat when that stands in the same town; The Shadow keeps its hideout. Asked now by `BotHomer` (and its cave check), `BotBolt.Help`/`Homeward`, `BotHerbs.Wood`, `BotHunter.Hunting`/`Feared`, `BotDelve.Rally`, `BotOutlaw.Release`, `BotAbodeBuyer` (where a bot looks for its own house), `TryPlace` (birth, revival, rescue, carry, unpark), `Rescue`'s "already home", the leash, `BotMindSight` ("Your camp is N tiles away") and Argus's `home` hand. Population-wide questions (`BotRoads`' flood, `BotGates`, `BotTowns`' reckoning, the city's errands, the Baron's harrow and stroll, the hideout's choice, the debugger's report) still ask `Where`. Cached five seconds per living bot (`BotResidence.CacheMs`), never for the dead (the outpost is the dead's home).
- *Decision (`BotResidence`, `BotResidenceStore` "BotResidences", shape 1):* a record per bot name — town, since, moves, the town last left — kept by the engine's persistence and held on the body (`BotMobile.Residence`). A name the store knows is born in that name's town, as it is handed that name's learning (`BotProgress`).
- *Decision (`BotSettle`):* a town is fit to live in when the gates reach it from home, a road in the book joins it to home, it has a bank (`NeedsBank`, on) and at least `LeastShops` (5) shopkeepers, counted once off its region with one spatial query; the home town is fit by definition. Towns reached only through a gate are out unless `GateTowns` (off) — nothing measures that walk; with the public moongates of build 317 it would let in Moonglow, Jhelom, Magincia and Skara Brae. The choice is weighed: the home town wants `HomeShare` (0.35), the other fit towns share the rest; weight = share / (1 + `SpreadWeight` (3) × residents / fair share), a bot on its way counted where it is going; × (1 + `GuildPull` (1.0) × the share of the bot's guild living there). A bot that walks there is measured against the road as a traveller is (`BotRoadbook.Asks` × `BotTraveller.Odds` 1.5 against `BotThreat.Power`) and must stand on land the gates join to the town; a town under a bar or quarantine is passed over.
- *Decision (who lives where, `BotRelocate`, once a minute over the population):* a guild seated abroad (its seat's nearest town is not home) — its members live there at once, as `BotSeat.Home` already made them; the classes in `StayHome` (Baron, Captain — the Baron's stroll is "the town at home", the drill field is `BotSchool.Ground` in Britain) live at home. Every other bot with no record (all of them on the first boot) is filed where home was until now and chooses once; a choice elsewhere is marked as a move. Newborns (`BotPopulation.Raise` → `BotResidence.Raised`, then `TryPlace`) are given their town before they are put down, so they are born there; the boot's own newborns are raised before the gates and roads answer (18:38:52 raised, 18:38:58 towns, 18:39:07 roads), so they are moved in once, when the towns are judged (`MoveIn`, within `NewbornMinutes` 10, their errand put down).
- *Decision (moving house, `BotMover` "Mover" on the Free rung → `BotResettle` "resettle"):* a marked bot, free, fit (`BotHunter.FitAt`), supplied, not in a company or underground, is offered the walk at `Prior` (10/min: above a journey's 8 and the walk home's 5, below any trade), unpaid, steadfast, the walk declared as the work as the walk home does. The road is `BotTravel`'s own deed held inside: the road is walked in the book, the guild is told, the traveller's clock is stamped. It lives in the new town from the moment the move is taken (a death on the road rises there; an offer changes nothing, C9). A mark not taken within `PendingMinutes` (60) is let go.
- *Decision (triggers):* over a stretch of `StretchHours` (2) in one town, a bot that gained less than `PoorGold` (150gp; the middling purse read 66gp at 18:58) in pack, bank and board **and** less than `PoorProgress` (0.01) of its trade is earning poorly; `DeathsToMove` (3) deaths within `DeathHours` (2) inside its own leash of home (counted in `BotMobile.OnDeath` with where it fell, before a delve's end moves the ghost) is dying where it lives. Either is a chance, `MoveOdds` (0.5), never within `MoveEveryHours` (4) of settling, never back to the town it last left (C11). A bot found at the end of a stretch living in a town not fit to live in (it left The Needle and still lives at Cove) chooses again without the draw. The stretch restarts after a rest out of the world.
- *Decision (`BotPopulation.Within(map, where)`):* the population's ground includes `BotTowns.Roam` round every town somebody lives in (`BotResidence.Around`), so a bot back from the save in its own town is not shut out of it before the gates answer. `BotBarred.Homely` never closes a box over a lived-in town's bank (`BotResidence.Homely`).
- *Decision (`BotShops.MaxShops` 96 → 256):* the spawn files put some 230 shopkeepers in the six mainland towns. Settable as `MaxShops` in `bot-shops.json`.
- *Also:* the "Residences:" summary line after "Travel:" (`BotBeat`); `"residence"` on every bot and `"residents"` on every town in the web snapshot; `"residence"` events on the stream; Argus's `reset` wipes the residences; module `Residence` (`bots.residence.enabled`), config `Configuration/bot-residence.json` (starter written empty), registered after Population and Travel; `regen-map.py` knows the folder.
- *Watch:*
  - boot: `Residences are on: each bot lives in a town of its own — home keeps 35 %`; from the second boot `Residences: where N bots live was read back from the save`;
  - `Residences: N of 18 towns are fit to live in: Britain (… shops, … banks, … healers), …; passed over: Cove (no bank), …` — Cove and Yew may fail on the bank; islands and the Lost Lands on the road;
  - `is moved into <Town>: from (…) to (…)` for the boot's newborns; `is born in <Town>, where N others of the population live` for `BotGrowth`'s;
  - `is the first bot marked to move house: to <Town>, settling: chose <Town> over Britain`, then `is moving house from Britain to <Town>: …; N live there now`, `took on resettle`, and BotTravel's `has walked from Britain to <Town> in N minutes`; `failed at resettle` / `could not reach … in 25 minutes`;
  - the 5-minute line `Residences: Britain N, Cove 15, Trinsic N, …; N born with a town (M away from home), … N marked to move (… settling, … for a poor living, … for deaths), … moves set out on, … arrived, … gave up on the road` — Britain should fall towards its share over hours, not in one boot: the weak stay until the road is theirs;
  - `Found N shopkeepers within 160 tiles of (<far town>)` should no longer read 0, and "(now N)" should stay under 256;
  - deaths a minute against the day's 0.3; deaths on the roads between towns; `found no shopkeeper selling X within its own reach` from far towns; the finished share (a resettle that gives up on the road is a failure).
- *Open (§6):* (1) the leash's own bypass `BotTowns.Within` (600 round every reachable town) makes every town shop part of every bot's leash, so build 301's "a shop beyond the leash is not the bot's shop" never fires for a town's shops — a resident of Minoc (no tailor) still walks to Britain for scissors; (2) residents abroad lose `BotRoads`' "how much further round by road" refinement, whose flood covers 640 tiles round Britain only; (3) `BotGround.MaxPlaces` (48 hearths, fires, counters) and `MaxSurveys` (64) are single budgets for the whole island — 19 hearths were known from Britain alone at 18:58; (4) members of the three seatless guilds choose one by one (softened by `GuildPull`); seating those guilds (`BotSeat.Choose` for existing guilds) would move them as whole guilds instead; (5) whether the island towns reached by moongate should be lived in (`GateTowns`); (6) The Needle is seated at Cove, which has no bank.

**29.09.2026 · build 320 (written by an Opus agent, merged by Opus) · Fires in the woods: bots make camp, sit round it, talk, and rest there; two passing bots stop for a word**
- *Why (Patrick's point 6 of 29.09.2026):* "More wandering, more chance meetings, more talk. Some bots may light a campfire in the woods and others join them; this counts as rest. Let them stand and chat with each other." Nothing on the shard brought two bots together except a company, a war or a queue at a counter, and nothing spoke except to announce work: of the 1,765 local lines in `bot-speech.log` between 17:00 and 19:00 every one rode on a `took:`/`finished:` of the bot's own work, the bank's `greet` occasion ("Well met, {name}") is said by no code at all — "Well met" appears nought times in 2.4 MB of speech — and a bot's one place to rest was an inn or its own house.
- *Decision (`BotCamp/`, new folder, `BotCampModule`, `Configuration/bot-camp.json`):* a registry of fires (`BotCamp.Fire`: a hearth tile, a ring of seats two tiles out, the engine's flame on it). Everything the engine owns is the engine's: the kindling is `Kindling`, laid on the hearth and double-clicked (`BotCamp.TryLight` → `Kindling.OnDoubleClick`, Camping rolled 0–100), what burns is `Campfire`, which dims at 60 s and is gone at 100 s unless a seated bot with a stick feeds it (`RelightWhenDim`, `TendTryMs` 1.5 s).
- *Decision (`BotKindle` "camp", `BotCamper`, Free rung, unpaid, steadfast):* a fire-lighter — `LighterShare` 0.5, dealt by an FNV hash of the name — on wild ground (not guarded, not a house, not underground, not `BotBarred.Holds`, quadrant `Safety` ≥ `LeastSafety` 0), tired (≥ `WearyFrom` 0.6 of its session, read from `BotRest.Records`), restless, or idle ≥ `IdleMinutes` 1, with no fire within `FireSpacing` 30, fewer than `MostFires` 6 burning, a means (sticks; logs and a fletcher's kit — `DefBowFletching`'s kindling; a knife or sword and a tree within `TreeReach` 12 — `BladedItemTarget`), a Camping that can rise (`BotCamp.Lights`: at the skill cap a player gains nothing and at 0 never catches), and nothing hostile within `HostileReach` 12 — looks cached `LookMs` 20 s — is offered camp at `Prior` 18 + up to `WearyWorth` 40 + `BoredWorth` 30 × boredom (`BotCamp.Claim`). Once in `EveryMs` 45 min per bot, started in `Taken`. It gathers up to `KindlingWant` 5, picks a hearth with ≥ `LeastSeats` 3 standable seats (every seat settled, `Ring`), strikes up to `MostFumbles` 60, keeps the fire `SitMinutes` 6 (±¼), banks it after `LonelyMs` 3 min with nobody come. In town with no kindling a fire-lighter is offered `BotRestock` for `KindlingBuy` 5 at a provisioner within `ShopReach` 40 (2 gp a stick).
- *Decision (`BotFireside` "fireside", `BotBeckon`, Free rung, unpaid, steadfast):* a free bot (no company, no fight, not tired, fit) within `JoinReach` 40 of an open fire, welcome by `Notoriety.Compute` both ways (no guild at war, no red, no criminal), is offered a seat at `Prior` 24 + the same weariness and boredom. The seat is held in `Taken` (not at the offer); it walks (`Hurries` false), sits on the ring (or where it stands after `SeatPatienceMs` 10 s within three tiles), faces the flame, and sits `GuestMinutes` 4 ±1.5. A keeper who leaves hands the fire to a seated bot with kindling (`Handed`), else it is banked. Once in `BotBeckon.EveryMs` 20 min per bot.
- *Decision (`BotCampTalk`):* round a fire of two or more, a line every `LineMs` 7 s + up to 4 s: a newcomer's `camp:greet` and the host's `camp:welcome`, then news — a walked road and its band (`BotRoadbook.Safety`), the worst square within `DangerReach` 250 and its dead (`BotQuad.WorstNear`), the speaker's stall or order or the board's best-paid want, its guild's war score or `BotGuilds.Aim` — or `camp:small`; `ReplyChance` 0.35 answered. At most `MostLinesEach` 5 per bot per fire; each line takes `CheerPerLine` 12 off every listener's boredom. Said with `BotVoice.Say(…, force: true)`; the 25 new occasions are added to the voice's bank only where `bot-voice.json` does not already name them.
- *Decision (`BotChat` "chat", `BotMeetings`):* once a second the camp looks at a slice of the population, each bot once in `EveryMs` 8 s; a free bot — idle or holding work that `Resumes`, not committed, no foe, not braving, not in a company, a fight, a duel, a cell or a dungeon, not in a guarded region (`InTowns` false) or a house, not met in `RestMs` 15 min — costs one `GetMobilesInRange` of `Reach` 3. With another such bot there (pair not met in `PairRestMs` 1 h, a pair that rolled no rests `MissRestMs` 2 min), `Chance` 0.2 presses both into `chat` (`BotWill.Press`, the errand put down and taken up again after): greet, answer, and `NewsChance` 0.7 a line of the same news; at most `MostMs` 30 s. The first beat finishes the walk in hand (`Journey.Finish`) — work leaves the journey alone, and a bot pressed mid-walk would otherwise walk on while "talking" (the delve hold's lesson, build 314).
- *Decision (rest, five delimited hooks in `BotRest`):* `Look` adds `BotCamp.Played(bot, minutes, hours)` — plain minutes for everybody else; for a bot seated at a warm fire and not tired, minus `minutes × Hours / ((LeastRestHours + MostRestHours) / 2) × RestShare` (1): the inn's rate, about 0.77 minutes of play back per minute sat for a five-hour player. In the free branch of a tired bot, `BotCamp.Beds` (secure: seated ≥ `SecureMs` 30 s, the engine's `Campfire` clock, seen in the last `BedGraceMs` 60 s, within `Campfire.SecureRange` 7) leaves the world from the fire before the house and the inn are asked; after `BotInns.ToInn`, `BotCamp.ToFire` sends a tired bot to the nearest open fire or makes camp where it stands (once in `ToFireRetryMs` 10 min) before the open ground. `Leave` writes "a campfire lit by X" into `record.Inn` (`BotCamp.Settle`), unpaid; `Return` gives `FireBuffShare` 1/6 of the rest as the well-rested regeneration (`BotCamp.Rested`) — half the paid bed's third, because the bed is bought and roofed (≈30 gp a night) and the fire costs a few two-gold sticks or none, and more than the unpaid bed's nothing because the camp is gathered, lit and kept secure, the engine's own condition for a camper's clean logout (`CampfireEntry.Safe`, `Bedroll`). No cheer: the talk was the cheer. Patrick's rule "offline only at an inn or one's own house" gains the fire and no fourth place.
- *Rule:* every deed here is unpaid, so its proposer asks every reason it fails first and a bot is not offered the same again for its `EveryMs` whatever came of the last (MAP §4, "taking the price off a piece of work takes its brake off too").
- *Watch:* boot `Camp is on: 50 % of the bots light fires …`, `Proposer Camper …`, `Proposer Fireside …`; `X the Y has lit a campfire at (x, y) with N seats round it (Camping 3.2); it means to keep it 6 minutes`; `a campfire lit by X at (x, y) is out after 7.4 minutes — it burned down: the evening is over; 2 came to it, 9 lines were said and 0 slept by it`; `X was pressed to chat: having a word with Y: met Y on the way; put down mine … to take up again` then `X took up mine … again after chat`; `X … leaves the world at (…) by a campfire lit by Y, unpaid after …h of play`, and on return `…, rested by a campfire lit by Y: regenerating until HH:mm`; the five-minute `Camp: N fires lit, M joined, K went offline at a fire, C chats (B burning now, S sitting at them); …` with every refusal by name; `[local]` lines in `logs/bot-speech.log`; `camp` and `meet` events on the stream. Numbers to watch against: fumbles per fire (a beginner ≈ 25), `Held` in the talk clause (voice off or no words), `BrokenOff` against `Finished` in the meetings, and "took up … again after chat" against "was pressed to chat".
- *Open:* `BotInns.LeftOutside` counts a fire's sleepers as it already counts a house's (`BotInns.Settle` is asked first); the `Camp:` count is the true one. Thirteen of forty-one leaves since 14:49 today were "on the open ground", and the three read were inside Britain — a fire does nothing for those; that is the inn's walk. "More wandering" is served only by the walk to a tree and to a fire: no stroll deed was added.

**29.09.2026 · build 320 (written by an Opus agent, merged by Opus) · Runes: a mage marks where it has stood, recalls there alone, and opens a gate there for its company**
- *Why (Patrick's order of 29.09.2026, point 7):* "a mage with Magery 40+ marks a rune (Mark) where it has been, and then Gate Travel opens a gate for the whole company; Recall — alone. A rune library in the guild hall and a pathfinder who got there by gate or boat. Instant transfer of a company anywhere they have stood." Until now every body crossed the island on foot. Today's sessions (14:00–19:00) have eight delves "came apart on the way to the Orc Caves" (seven "1 left of 5"; Hilde at 18:22 after 12.0 minutes' march, Brokk and Keyleth at 18:36 after 10.6 and 10.8) and a dozen sweeps "came apart on the way to (x, y): 2 left". The long road is where companies are lost.
- *What the engine allows (read, not assumed):* UOR (`expansion.json` Id 2). `MagerySpell._requiredSkill` gives Recall 30–70 from a book, Mark 50–90, Gate Travel 60–100 (a scroll: two circles lower, Mark 30–70, Gate 40–80); so at Magery 40 a book Recall lands one time in four, Mark only from a scroll, Gate not at all. `SpellHelper` travel rules forbid Mark, Recall-to and Gate-to inside every Felucca dungeon region: a mouth's rune stands on the island side of the teleporter, never on the landing inside. `Spell.CheckSequence` takes the reagents before the skill check (a fizzle costs herbs, not mana). The gate is `GateTravelMoongate`, thirty seconds in this era, two-way; a gate in a guarded town to a place outside one asks a confirmation gump (`Moongate.BeginConfirmation`) that a bot has no screen for. No shopkeeper in this era sells a runebook (`SBScribe`'s line is commented out); `SBMage` sells blank recall runes at 15gp.
- *Decision — marking (`BotRunes/BotMark.cs`: `BotMark`, `BotMarker`):* a rune-mage (`BotRunes.LeastMagery` 40) with a blank, standing at a place its guild holds no rune for, is offered the mark on the Free rung: its seat (`BotSeat.Home`, within `BotMarker.SeatReach` 40), a cave mouth (the island end of a `BotGates` gate into a dungeon, within `MouthReach` 40), or the town whose box it stands in (`BotTowns.Of`) — so the pathfinder is simply the first mage of the guild to arrive, however it came (a journey, a boat, a gate, a party walking out). The engine is asked before the offer (`BotRunes.Ready`: book or scroll, chance ≥ `LeastChance` 0.2, mana, reagents, recovery), so a book Mark below 50 is never offered to fail. The deed walks to the nearest tile the engine would let a rune be marked, recalled and gated to (`BotRunes.Landable`: no house, no teleporter within a tile, the travel rules), casts `MarkSpell`, aims its target at the blank (`Target.Invoke`), and files the place. `Prior` 30/min, unpaid, steadfast, `CapMs` 3 min, `Tries` 3 with `RetryMs` 4 s, then the place rests `RestMs` 20 min for that mage.
- *Decision — knowledge and the library (`BotRuneShelf`, `BotRuneStore` "BotRunes", `BotRuneLibrary`):* the guild's places (name, kind, spot, marker, uses; at most `Shelf` 16, the least used dropped first, never the seat) are kept in a GenericPersistence store, so a restart keeps what every guild knows. The library is a runebook "the library of {guild}" in the hall's chest (`BotAbode.Chest`) when there is a hall, else in the keeper's pack (the guild's best mage, else its head), written from the store every `EveryMs` 5 s and moved into the chest when a hall goes up. The marked rune itself goes into the marker's own book ("{name}'s runes", made on first need, bound without an entitlement); a rune in a chest takes nobody anywhere. A rune-mage at the library (`Reach` 16 of the chest, `KeeperReach` 8 of the keeper) is lent a copy of every rune its book lacks, **a blank each** — copying is not an engine operation, the blank is its price.
- *Decision — blanks (`BotRuneBuy`, `BotRuneBuyer`):* a rune-mage that knows any of the three spells keeps `Blanks` 3; short, it is offered the nearest shop selling them (`BotShops.Nearest`), funded as a delve's supplies are (`BotProvision.Fund`: its purse, the guild's chest, its guildmates); a failed trip rests 10 min. What is bought is bound at once, or the unloading sells it.
- *Decision — learning (`BotGrimoire.Missing` → `BotRunes.Wanted`):* after the class's own first spells, a mage at `LeastMagery` wants Recall, then Mark, and at `GateMagery` 60 Gate Travel, before the rest of its circles; `Learn` false turns it off. Without it the book fills lowest id first and reaches Recall after thirty spells.
- *Decision — recall (`BotRecall`, hooked in `BotTravel.Advance`, `BotHomeward.Advance`, `BotRestock.Advance`):* a far walk asks first. A rune-mage more than `Far` 200 tiles off, holding a rune within its arrival (or `Near` 12) of where it is going that saves at least `LeastSaved` 150 tiles, and allowed by the engine (`RecallFrom`/`RecallTo`), stands and casts `RecallSpell` on the runebook entry (the runebook gump's path: skill, mana, reagents). A fizzle is tried again up to 3 times, then the walk takes over for the rest of that walk; a mage that could not cast is asked again every `ReconsiderMs` 30 s while it walks. A recalled journey does not count its road as walked (`BotRoadbook.Between` instead of `Walked`).
- *Decision — company gate (`BotPassage`, hooked in `BotDelve.Descend`/`Marching`/`Drop`, `BotSweep.Calling`/`Patrolling`/`Drop`, `BotEnlist.Holding`):* when a delve marches by the mouth, or a sweep sets out, and a member can cast Gate Travel and holds a rune within `GateNear` 60 of where the company goes (the mouth's island end; the square), the passage takes the leader's beats and, through the enlistment's hold, the members'. The mage casts `GateTravelSpell` on its entry where it stands; the members walk to the gate and are put through by the engine's own use of it (`Moongate.EndConfirmation`: range one, same map, not casting — the gump never asked); the leader crosses **last**, when nobody is left to wait for or at `CrossMs` 22 s; then the company's own march goes on from the far side and the delve's hold at the landing regroups it at the mouth. A sweep first waits `GatherMs` 60 s for its levy to stand round the captain. A fight at the muster or short mana waits `WaitMs` 60 s. Members through wait three tiles off the far gate (standing on it, a step takes them back). Whoever has not reached the gate when the leader crosses stays on the near side and is left to the march's own hold (`MarchLost`). Should the gate close with members through and the leader still on the near side, the leader walks to them (`RejoinMs` 10 min) and they wait where they landed. Three failed casts, or a mage that cannot cast, and the company marches by road as before.
- *Summary (`BotBeat`, every five minutes):* "Runes: N marked (Britain 1, the seat of The Blade 1, the mouth of Despise 1), M recalls saving T tiles, K gates opened, L through them; …places held…; …libraries…; …marker…; …blanks…; recalls: …; gates: …".
- *Expected:* nothing visible for the first hours of the wiped world: few mages stand at 40 Magery, and Recall, Mark and Gate Travel are fourth, sixth and seventh circle — no shop sells them, a scribe must write them. First: "took on acquire" for Recall and Mark by mages at 40+, "took on blanks", then the first mark at a seat; recalls home once a seat is marked and a copy lent; gates only once a mage reaches about 68 Magery (20 % from a book) or holds a Gate Travel scroll at 48+.
- *Watch:* boot "Runes are on: a mage of Magery 40+ marks where its guild holds no rune …" and, after the first save, "Runes: N places the guilds hold runes for read back from the save"; "{Name} the {Class} is the first rune-mage offered a mark: {Place} for {Guild}"; "{Name} the {Class} marked a rune for {Place} at (x, y) with {M} Magery; {Guild} holds runes for {N} places"; "{Guild} has a rune library now, in its hall's chest" / "carried by {Name}"; "{Name} the {Class} was lent {N} runes at {Guild}'s library and holds {M} now"; "{Name} the {Class} recalled to {Place} instead of walking {T} tiles (home); {L} left to walk" against "… could not recall to {Place} in 3 tries (the spell fizzled) and walks {T} tiles instead"; "{Mage} will open a gate for {Leader}'s company at (x, y) to {Place}, …", "{Mage} opened a gate at (x, y) to {Place} for {Leader}'s company of {N}", "{Leader}'s company went through {Mage}'s gate to {Place}: {K} and the leader through, {L} left on the near side, {S} tiles of march to the mouth of {Dungeon} saved", and then the delve's own "has led N into {Dungeon} by its mouth after M minutes' march" with M near nought. Counters that should read nought: the gates line's "found back on the near side" and "gates closed half through".
- *Risks:* the travel-spell priority changes what mages spend on (three scrolls before the rest of their circles); the library lends by copy (a blank each), which is a rule of this shard and not of the engine; a library found missing (a restart for a keeper's book, a burglar at the chest) is written again from the store; members are put through the gate by `EndConfirmation`, the engine's own confirmation path, rather than by stepping on the tile.
- *Code:* `Projects/BotAIv2/BotRunes/` (new: `BotRunes`, `BotRuneShelf`+`BotRuneStore`, `BotRuneLibrary`, `BotMark`+`BotMarker`, `BotRuneBuy`+`BotRuneBuyer`, `BotRecall`, `BotPassage`, `BotRunesModule`, `Configuration/bot-runes.json`); hooks in `BotCore`, `BotBeat`, `BotHomeward`, `BotTravel`, `BotRestock`, `BotDelve`, `BotSweep`, `BotEnlist`, `BotGrimoire`; `regen-map.py` knows the folder.
- *Status:* **active** (unmeasured).

**29.09.2026 · build 319 (written by Opus) · The gates' lands follow the graph's recount; a death is filed where it fell; miners walk to a floor, not to the rock; a sweep gathers before it marches**
- *Measured on 318 (19:12–19:26):* 309 of 338 endings finished (91 %), 14 failed, 7 dropped, 8 died; five walkers through a moongate; seven levied members released ("went on without it"). Weak trades: enlist 43 %, mend 54 %, mine 88 %.

**29.09.2026 · build 308 (written by Fable) · The hang, found: the long tier handed the goal a parent it had never relaxed**
- *What the bound showed (13:19, build 307):* "1 parent chains found looping and cut (the last at node 0)". The chain ran into node 0, whose parent is 0 — an array default, never set in that search.
- *Where (`StrategicPlanner.Search`):* when the start and the goal lie in one region (`rs == rg`), the search relaxed the goal straight from each goal-border node that the start could reach (`RelaxGoal(g, toHere + c, n)`) without ever relaxing `n` itself, so `n`'s parent was whatever an earlier search had left there, or nought; `Corridor` walked the goal's chain into it and round node 0 for ever. The danger hook made it fire: a heavy penalty pushes the medium tier over its budget on short routes too, and a same-region route on the long tier is exactly this branch — which the constant-band and moving-band tests never took, because their routes crossed the river.
- *Decision:* `n` is relaxed from the start first (`Relax(graph, n, toHere, s, …)`), then the goal from `n`; the chain is goal, node, start. `SameRegionOnTheLongTier_ComesBack` in `DangerHookTests` forces the long tier on forty same-region routes with a medium budget of one expansion and asserts no cycle; the bound of 306 stays as a belt.
- *Rule:* a parent handed to a search must have been relaxed in that search; a chain is only as good as its weakest link's parent.

**29.09.2026 · build 306 (written by Fable) · The planners bound their parent-chain walks; the hook is on again**
- *Why:* the loop hung twice in `StrategicPlanner.Corridor`'s walk up the parent chain with the danger hook on, and a grid does not reproduce it: `DangerHookTests` (new, in `UOContent.Tests`) routes 480 pairs across a river with a constant penalised band at four strengths and 320 more with a band that moves between routes, and every route comes back. Whatever loops the chain on the real map is not found by reading; it is bounded instead.
- *Decision (`StrategicPlanner.Corridor`, `HierarchicalPlanner.Unwind`, `Cycles`, `LastCycleNode`):* a chain longer than the graph has nodes is a loop; the walk stops, the loop is counted, the corridor is what was gathered (the hierarchical path is emptied). The navigation summary prints "N parent chains found looping and cut (the last at node K)".
- *Decision (`BotDanger.Running` true):* the hook is on again behind the bound.
- *Watch:* "parent chains found looping" — the first non-zero is the evidence the reading lacked, with the node; the watchdog on the log.
- *Measured (13:19, build 307):* "1 parent chains found looping and cut (the last at node 0)" — the chain ran into node 0, whose parent is 0: a parent entry never set in that search (the array's default), reached through a node that was. The loop is at node 0, not a cycle among relaxed nodes; the search that hands a chain to node 0 is the next thing to find (a start node relaxed with a parent of 0 rather than the start sentinel, or a stale parent read across searches).

**29.09.2026 · build 305 (written by Fable) · The danger hook is off: the second hang, with its stack**
- *What happened:* the loop hung again at 12:22:41 on build 304, two minutes after its start, with `BarredCost` at eight hundred and the overflow guard of 302 in place. This time the stack was taken (`dotnet-stack report -p <pid>`, installed for it): the main thread was inside `StrategicPlanner.Corridor`, called from `Search` after the goal was reached, from `BotJourney.Draw` — the unwind of the parent chain `for (node = _parent[g]; node >= 0 && node != s; node = _parent[node])`, which ends only if the chain ends. Both hangs followed a shop survey at a far point ((1746, 1041) and (2004, 788), by the bog) — a long route from there with the hook on.
- *Decision (`BotDanger.Running` false):* the hook is off until the cycle is reproduced offline. The overflow guard of 302 stays; it was not the cause.
- *Why the cycle (the hypothesis):* the strategic planner's region-internal edges are cached shortest paths (`Ensure`); with a per-node penalty added at relaxation on top of them the costs a search sees are no longer consistent with the cached edges, and a node can be re-parented onto its own descendant; a parent chain with a loop in it never reaches the start.
- *Next:* a test in `UOContent.Tests` for the tiered planner with a `Danger` hook that penalises a band of nodes heavily, many random routes, a timeout; then either the penalty goes into the cached edges (rebuild regions when the danger changes) or the corridor unwind guards against a loop (a visited set) and the search refuses re-parenting of closed nodes.
- *Rule:* a hang is diagnosed with a stack, not a guess — `dotnet-stack report -p` takes ten seconds and named the method; the guess of 302 (an int overflow) was wrong.

**29.09.2026 · build 302 (written by Fable) · The loop hung on a cost that overflowed; the planners refuse one**
- *What happened:* `BotDanger.BarredCost` was set to five thousand at 11:32 (dial) and 11:34 (build 301); the log stopped at 11:38:15 with the process spinning at a full core for twelve minutes, no save in progress (the last completed at 11:35:01). The world lost the three minutes after it. Killed and restarted by hand at 11:55.
- *Why (the hypothesis, not proved by a dump):* five thousand tiles a node is five hundred thousand cost units; a route through a bar two hundred tiles across crosses tens of nodes, and the planners' costs are ints. An overflowed cost is negative, a negative cost always improves on its neighbour, and a node that always relaxes is a search that never ends. The medium planner's expansion budget did not save it because the relax loop is inside one expansion's edge sweep.
- *Decision (`NavCost.Unaffordable` = int.MaxValue / 4; both planners' `Relax`):* a cost negative or past a quarter of the int range is refused. `BarredCost` back to eight hundred.
- *Rule:* a penalty hook is a number added inside somebody else's arithmetic; its ceiling is theirs, not ours.
- *Watch:* the loop's own timing line; "the roads read the danger" counts; no log gap.

Printed in the "Getting about" line as "the roads read the danger: N nodes asked, B bloodied, R barred".

**29.09.2026 · build 285 (written by Fable) · Killing fields closed on the count of the dead; newcomers born into the role a guild lacks; no spec sewing off a counter; scissors a trade tool**
- *Why (measured on 284, 03:20–05:05, the first two hours after the wipe):* 2578 of 3110 endings finished (83 %), 215 of them deaths, 225 failed, 92 dropped. The deaths sat in six fixed spawns round Britain: seven under one reaper at (1640–1680, 1400–1440) — the wood the woodcutters are sent to — twenty-four to the wraiths and spectres of the graveyard sixty tiles west of the home ground at (1440, 1470), the trolls and harpies of the Yew road, the ettins and trolls south at (1240–1400, 1960), gargoyles and ettins north-east. Seventy died in flight and thirty-one more when their work was not taken up again after one. The quarantine of 281 asked only whether the killer was the plague or something past 30,000, and a novice is killed by an ettin. Of the four guilds three had nobody to make anything: two crafters in the whole population, both in The Blade, and one architect outside every guild. The tailors bought 2080 cloth for 4160gp and sewed oilcloth at a loss of 23–35gp a stint that nobody bought (286 things on the stalls, 570 wants finding them too dear) — the largest single outflow to the shopkeepers while 25,296 asks at a door were turned away for want of ten bandages. The weaver refused 1240 of 1265 asks "without scissors": the crafters had none, a crafter back from its death restocks scissors at 8 a minute (universal tools are nobody's trade), and the population bought 191 pairs meanwhile.
- *Decision (`BotBarred.Fell`, from `BotMobile.OnDeath`):* every bot death is counted; `KillingDeaths` (3) within `QuarantineHalf` (45) of each other inside `KillingWindowMs` (30 min) declare a killing field and close it as a quarantine for `QuarantineMs` (2 h), whoever did the killing, under the same `Homely` exemption for the home ground, halls and seats. The plague rule stands. `Fields` counts them; the ground summary now says how many quarantines were declared, how many are in force and how many choices they turned.
- *Decision (`BotGuilds.Lacking`, `BotGrowth.LeastToWant` 3, `ByNeed`):* a guild of three or more bots with nobody of a role gets the next newcomer in that role — a producer first, a medic second — drawn by the mix's weights among that role's classes (Crafter or Healer when the mix lists none); the newcomer's own joining (`Roomiest`) seats it where its role is thinnest.
- *Decision (`BotTailor.BuysCloth` off, `NoBoughtCloth`):* cloth is not bought over a counter to sew on spec. Spec work is for the pack's own cloth (the weaver's) and for hide. Nothing changes for orders, which were always leather.
- *Decision (`BotShopper.Wanting`):* scissors count as a trade tool for whoever carries a sewing kit, so their restock scores as a kit's does (`BotRestock.Spare` 180) instead of 12.

**26.09.2026 · build 268 (written by Opus) · The medium tier's search leans towards the goal; the graph read back from disk at boot**
- *Why:* a step costs the same straight or diagonal, so the straight-line estimate leaves wide plateaus of routes of exactly equal cost, and A* opens every node of a plateau before it leaves it. On the live map a medium route took 2.1 ms on average and 7 ms for one in twenty (build 267's `navbench`), against the 1 ms the design asked for.
- *Decision (`HierarchicalPlanner.TieBreak`, 1000):* the estimate in the open list's priority gains one part in 1000 of itself, so of two nodes on a plateau the one nearer the goal is opened first. A route found is at most one part in 1000 dearer than the best. Tests: the 13 of the tiers, all pass; on the grid tests the expansions fell only a little.
- *And:* this is the first boot after build 267 wrote the graph of Felucca to disk (36 MB, 151 ms off the loop).
- *Watch:* "the graph of Felucca was read from disk", with the loop's milliseconds to put it in place, and no "could not be read"; then `navbench 300 500 60` against build 267's 2.1 ms mean and 7 ms p95.
- *Seen (15:56–15:59):* the graph was read from disk a second after boot and put in place in 234 ms of the loop; the 84 clusters by houses were drawn again, and the graph was whole two seconds after boot, in 970 ms of the loop (a full draw: 105 s, 17.6 s of the loop). It came out the same as a full draw: 285,550 nodes, 2,478,736 edges, 1,216 components. The regions were built 14 s after boot. The lean did not pay: on build 267's 300 pairs (the benchmark's seed is fixed), 1,959,599 nodes were opened against 1,969,656, half a percent fewer, while a route took 2.66 ms on average and 9.4 ms at the 95th percentile against 2.07 and 7.0. The first benchmark after the boot was slower still (3.1 ms) and 10 of its 2,649 legs failed the precise search, 0 on the rerun: the step cache is cold after a boot that reads the graph instead of drawing it. Why the time rose while the work fell is not known yet: a loop just after boot, or a graph read rather than drawn, are the candidates. The lean stays; it is not the lever for the 1 ms.

**26.09.2026 · build 267 (written by Opus) · The graph kept on disk between boots; a benchmark of the tiers on the live map**

- *Decision (`NavGraphFile`):* once the graph is whole and its components counted, a copy of its arrays is taken on the loop and a worker thread writes it to `Data/Pathfinding/navgraph-<map>.nvg`, never while the world saves. At the next boot a worker thread reads it, if it was drawn from the same map files (the step cache's own fingerprint, `StepCacheFile.ComputeFingerprint`), and the loop puts it in place (`NavGraph.Restore`); the bake waits for the read. The clusters by a house when the file was written, and those by a house standing now, are torn down and drawn again. Setting `pathfinding.tiered.persist` (on). Test: a graph written and read back plans the same routes at the same cost, a file of other map files is refused, and a house raised on the restored graph is drawn again (13 tests, all pass).
- *And (the door's `navbench n radius checked`):* n random pairs of standable tiles within radius of home, routed over the graph — how many found, direct, unreachable, over budget or handed to the long tier; the milliseconds (mean, 95th percentile, worst); for the first routes found, every leg walked by the precise search, and the route's length set against the precise search's own plan from end to end at three times its ceiling.
- *Watch:* "the graph of Felucca was written to disk" after this boot's bake, and "was read from disk" at the next boot, with the loop's milliseconds to put it in place.

**26.09.2026 · build 264 (ordered by Patrick ~14:50, written by Opus) · Tiered navigation in the engine: the medium tier drawn over the whole map, floors and bridges apart, and the bots walking it**
- *Patrick's order (26.09.2026):* "the goal of today is the implementation of the different levels of path search", with a design document (`uo-tiered-pathfinding.md`): Short (the precise tile search), Medium (hierarchical A* over 16-tile clusters), Long (128-tile regions, portals), one cost model, components for "unreachable" without searching, built on the step cache's masks and strata, houses as an overlay.
- *Seen on build 263 (the chart of 262, walked):* in its first ten minutes 12,805 searches cost 13.5 s (1.35 s a minute against 12.5 before), 6.8 % partial against 38 %, 5,412 legs, none failed. And the agent reading the walker found where the first cut was weak: the route lived in one slot of the journey, so a fight pushed on top threw it away; a failed leg and a Sealed plan switched the "no closer" measures from road to straight line mid-walk; a goal that walked on counted as a reroute; a company's stations were re-issued every 1.5 s and each drew a route; a far bank twenty tiles across a river was never routed; and three errands' own watches (supply, hire, dig) still measured straight. Two supply runs to The Lantern's counter failed "stopped closing" in the first window.
- *Decision, in the engine (`Projects/UOContent/Engines/Pathing/Tiered`):*
  - `NavCost`: a step is 100, straight or diagonal (the engine's delay does not depend on it), a diagonal 1 more to break ties; the estimate is Chebyshev, never more than the truth.
  - `NavTerrain`: the ground from the engine's step probe, and its multi-aware form in any sector a house touches (`StepProbe.ComputeStandableSurfaceZsWithMultis`, new).
  - `NavWindow`: a cluster and the ring round it, probed lazily; every standable surface of a cell is its own stratum (up to 4); a step lands on the neighbour's surface within 3 of where the engine says, and a diagonal needs both flanks.
  - `NavGraph` (L1): entrances across each cluster edge per pair of strata, one gate in the middle of a run of at most 6, two at its ends when longer; directed edges; intra-cluster costs by a flood from each node. Drawn a cluster at a time outward from home, 8 ms every 50 ms; a cluster whose ground changes is torn down with its four edges and drawn again, node ids stable (`MarkDirty`). Components by union-find once complete.
  - `HierarchicalPlanner` (Medium): the ends joined to their clusters by a flood (forward from the start, backward to the goal), `Direct` when joined inside one cluster, `Unreachable` from the components without searching, else A* with ties to the larger cost so far; one point a cluster back. Windows of probed clusters kept in a cache of 64. A gate a walker could not pass is shunned for 10 minutes.
  - `NavigationService`: one graph a map, `Prepare`, `Route`, `GroundChanged`, `Shun`, settings `pathfinding.tiered.*` and `pathfinding.medium.*`.
  - `BaseHouse`: a house raised, moved or taken down tells the navigation (`GroundChanged`), beside the spawn-cache call already there.
  - Tests (`UOContent.Tests/Tests/Engines/Pathing/Tiered`, 9, all pass): an open field within 10 % of a tile Dijkstra oracle; a wall with a gap; a sealed wall answered unreachable with no node expanded; a bridge deck over a road, the two levels kept apart; a one-way drop walked down and not up; pending before drawn; a house raised and taken down with no node leaked; 295 random routes among random walls, 5.4 % over the oracle on average, 18.6 % at worst, never cheaper, never a false "unreachable".
- *Decision, in the bots:*
  - The route belongs to its errand (`BotErrand.Route`), so a fight keeps its own and the road underneath survives it.
  - `BotJourney.Leg` asks `NavigationService` first and the old chart only where the graph cannot answer yet; routes a far target, a live route, and a near one the road map says lies round a river (`RoundTiles` 40) once the straight plan stops closing; never a company's station or sweep; counts only failed legs and strays as reroutes.
  - A leg that proves Sealed hands the beat to the straight plan instead of an empty one; a starved or constrained search shuns no gate.
  - "The ground has no way there": an errand whose target the graph proves unreachable is dropped at once when it is further than `DirectTiles`.
  - Progress is measured by the route while one is held, and every measure — the journey's, the will's, supply's, hire's, dig's — starts its best again when a route is drawn (`RouteStamp`).
  - `BotRoads` starts the graph from home; "Navigation:" beside "Getting about:" every five minutes; the door's `nav`.
- *Not yet:* the Long tier (128-tile regions, teleporters and moongates, a route cache), the graph saved to disk, the engine's own mobiles on the tiers.
- *Watch:* the "Navigation:" line (clusters drawn and the loop's milliseconds, routes by status, window hits); "Getting about:" against build 263; "the ground has no way there" drops, to be read one by one for a false one.
- *Undo:* `pathfinding.tiered.enable: false` in `modernuo.json` (the old chart answers every route again); `dial BotJourney.DirectTiles 100000` walks everything straight.

**26.09.2026 · build 263 (ordered by Patrick ~14:15, written by Opus) · Far walks go over the chart, a leg at a time; work across a river is priced by the road**
- *Seen on build 262 (the chart in shadow, 14:26):* the chart was drawn in 234 ms of the loop over 3 s — 44,696 nodes, 22,380 gates on 6,561 squares of 16 tiles, 490,500 ways. Asked through the door: from the east bank (1168, 1384) to The Lantern's door (1084, 1406), 123 points, about 1,457 steps for 84 straight, 31,102 nodes expanded in 10 ms, and the planner walked each of the first five legs in at most 0.1 ms (it had failed the whole walk at 150 ms); from home to the same door 130 points in 5.6 ms; from the bank to home 16 points in 0.12 ms; from The Hammer's hall to home 24 points in 0.29 ms.
- *Decision:*
  - `BotJourney.Leg`: an errand whose target is further than `DirectTiles` (24) is walked over the chart's route (`BotChart.Route`), drawn once per errand and goal: each plan goes to the furthest point of the next few that follow within `LegTiles` (24) of road, at `BotArrival.Within(LegReached)` (3). The route is drawn again when the goal walks off by half a leg or the bot has strayed `StrayTiles` (24) from its point; after `MostReroutes` (4) the errand is walked straight, as before.
  - `BotWalk.PlanLeg`: a leg that proves shut, or plans twice without getting nearer along the route, is not a verdict on the target — its gate is shunned on the chart and the route drawn again (`LegFailed`, `BotChart.Shun`). The escalation, the far side and the stranded ceiling stay for walks planned straight.
  - Progress is measured along the route while one is walked: the journey's "no closer" count (`BotJourney.Distance`) and the will's watch over a walk that has stopped closing (`BotWill`, `BotJourney.RoadLeft`), which measured straight would call the road round a river a walk going the wrong way.
  - `BotAppraisal`: the walk to work is priced by the road — the straight tiles plus how much further round one end lies than the other (`BotRoads.Farther`) — so work across a river, which a bot will now actually walk to, is no longer taken as near.
- *Not changed:* the harrow's levy still passes over bots across a river from the muster (`BotHarrow.Reaches`, build 261): a thousand steps is more than a five-minute muster; `BotPlot` still refuses new ground across a river.
- *Watch:* "Getting about:" (searches, their milliseconds and the loop's share, partial and "no nearer" counts) against the session 13:16–14:05 (72,294 searches, 562 s of 2,700, 27,739 partial, 11,141 no nearer); "no way through" and "no way round" failures; the walker's legs and failed legs; the chart's routes, their milliseconds and shunned gates.
- *Undo:* `dial BotJourney.DirectTiles 100000` walks everything straight again; `dial BotChart.Running false` stops the chart at the next boot.

**26.09.2026 · build 262 (ordered by Patrick ~14:15, written by Opus) · The coarse chart: a two-level way of finding a path, drawn and asked, not yet walked**
- *Patrick's order (26.09.2026):* "maybe it is time to find another way of finding a path — if they are banging into a rock, build the way roughly over the squares that can be crossed; we have used your research for almost a month and the bots are still terribly dull."
- *Seen:* in the session 13:16–14:05 the planner ran 72,294 searches for 562 s of the loop (21 %); 27,739 ended partial and 11,141 of those no nearer than they began. The Lantern's company, called at its hall's door (1084, 1406) three times between 14:05 and 14:14, failed each time "no way round it was found in 150ms" from the east bank — 90 tiles off, about 1,170 steps round by the south. Every change of the month before was to the planner's ceiling, the notes and the refusals; none changed the method.
- *Decision (this build, measurement first):*
  - `BotRoads` keeps, per tile at the height it was first reached, the steps a body may take from it — the engine's step mask, a diagonal only with both flanks — as its flood already reads them (`Lend`).
  - `BotChart` (new, `BotMovement`): squares of `Side` 16 tiles over the road map's square; a gate for each run of tiles that step across the edge between two squares both ways (two gates, one near each end, for a run longer than `LongGate` 8), with a node on each side; inside each square, a small flood from each node gives the steps to the square's other nodes. Drawn after the road map on its timer, in slices of `SliceMs` 8. `Route` is an A* over the nodes (the start and goal joined to their squares' nodes by the same small flood; Chebyshev distance as the estimate), and answers one point a square. A gate a leg could not pass can be shunned (`Shun`, `ShunMs` 10 minutes, `ShunCost` 400).
  - The door: `chart` (its state), `chart <bot> <x> <y>` and `chart <x1> <y1> <x2> <y2>` (the route, its length, and whether the planner walks its first five legs).
  - Walking does not use it yet: the next build puts the walker on it once the routes are seen to be right.
- *Watch:* the "Chart:" line at the boot (nodes, gates, time on the loop); routes asked through the door from the east bank to The Lantern's door.
- *Undo:* `dial BotChart.Running false`.

**26.09.2026 · build 261 (written by Opus, the first minutes of build 260) · A muster calls only who can walk to it; a band brings the allies it was called with**
- *Seen (14:05–14:11):* The Lantern's company for (1065, 1425) was called at its hall's door (1084, 1406) at 14:05:57, as build 260 meant it to be, and failed twice: Ysolt, 90 tiles east of the door at (1171, 1382), "found no way round in 150ms" at 14:08:30 and again at 14:10:39. And a band (`BotBand`), which `BotMuster` calls only when the bot and the allies by it together can take what one could not, was refused by build 260's wall on the one bot's strength ("5069, 5.9 times the 864 going there").

Where the road map cannot say, it can.
  - `BotBand.Brings`: the strength of the bot and the allies by it when the band was called (`BotThreat.OurPower`), until the squad stands.

**26.09.2026 · build 260 (answered by Patrick ~13:45, written by Opus) · A guild clears the spawn by its own hall with its own company, as a duty; ground is closed by the fight there, several times what goes, and no longer by a count of the dead**
- *Patrick's answer (26.09.2026), on halls standing beside live spawns once the world was awake:* (a) no moving halls away: "they put it there, so let them defend their own ground — that is their duty"; (b) "the guild clears the spawn by its hall with a company, as the Baron clears dire squares — yes, they gather themselves and clear it themselves"; (c) bots "go round only extremely dangerous places, like the swamp, where the hostility of the forces is several times theirs".
- *Seen (13:16–13:58, the first forty minutes awake):* 127 deaths, 41 of them to other bots in the wars, 85 to creatures — ratmen 19 round The Lantern's hall at 1082,1402, gargoyles 14 round The Hammer's at 1754,1482. The Lantern was offered the harrowing of its own squares by its hall some 150 times and took it three times: the harrow was reckoned at the Baron's corrected rate (38–41/min) and lost to a restock (179/min), peddling and hunts; Brannoc's company mustered at the population's home (1440,1470), 375 tiles off beyond the river, and failed "no way through"; Ysolt's mustered at Britain's gate (1369,1534), gathered six of six from any guild, marched on (1065,1395) and failed on the road; every other offer was refused "lies in or beside ground where 4.6 bots have died lately, against 3.0 that close it to everything but running". The same count of the dead was the first veto printed for 150 restocks and 72 reclaims. Of the 83 bots a creature killed, 19 had met something three times their company's strength.
- *Decision 1 (the guild's own company, `BotReeve`, `BotHarrow`):*
  - musters at its hall's door (`BotFeud.MusterPoint`, the war company's), not at a town's gate or the population's home;
  - levies the guild's own members wherever they are, and nobody else; the wanted company is at most the guild's fighters (`BotReeve.Fighters`), at least `Least` (3);
  - is a duty, not a trade: `Unpaid`, reckoned at `BotHarrow.DutyPrior` 300/min — above supplies and ordinary work, below a war's call (400) and the defence of the yard (700);
  - takes in the squares round the hall's own that nobody holds (`BotReeve.Ring` 1, the hall's square and the eight round it; `BotReeve.Warden`); the Baron leaves such ground to a guild with at least `Least` fighters alive;
  - nobody goes without its supplies: the leader is asked (`BotReeve` `Unsupplied`), and every harrow's levy — the Baron's too — passes over a bot below its entry threshold (`BotHarrow` `Unsupplied`; build 259, "an entry threshold for everybody").
- *Decision 2 (the ground, `BotPeril.Overwhelms`, K = `Overwhelm` 3.0):* work is refused only where the hostile strength is three times what goes there or more — the bot, or the company it is in (`BotQuad.Strength`), or the company a harrow or a company prowl will raise (`BotDeed.Brings`). The hostile strength of a place (`BotPeril.Hostility`) is the larger of the wild creatures that attack unprovoked within `HostileReach` 14 tiles now (the strongest in full and the rest at 0.4, `BotThreat`'s reckoning of a fight) and what the spawners near keep within sight (`BotLairs.MetFight`), kept per 8-tile cell for 10 seconds. A bot already within 14 tiles of the place is not walking into it. Running away is never refused. It replaces both counts of the dead in `BotAppraisal.Weigh` (`BotPeril.Closes` 3, all work; `BotPeril.Lethal` 2, ordinary work) and the count in `BotHunter` that made ground company ground; the harrow proposers ask the same question with the same numbers (`BotHarrow.Expected`), so an offer is not one the auction then refuses at every review.
- *Not changed, and why:* the squares' asked strength (`BotQuad.Muscle`, Patrick's table of 03.09.2026) and the walls built on it (`Dares`, `Together`, the prowl's gate); the hand-set bars (`BotBarred`, the plague bog among them); routing, which avoids nothing (`BotJourney.AvoidDanger` has no caller). These are for Patrick.
- *Also (`BotToll.Nearest`):* a stranger listed as hunting a guild's land is offered to its wardens only while still on it; the list is made every `LookMs`, and Talia of The Blade took and finished the same ward five times in one second at 13:40:24 ("had left the land before it was told").
- *Watch:* `BotReeve` and `BotHarrower` summaries (offered, unsupplied, overwhelmed), the guild's musters at its hall and whether they march and empty the square; the deaths round the halls; the auction's refusals line ("the hostile strength … times what was going there").
- *Undo:* `dial BotPeril.KeepsOut false` lifts the new wall (the counts of the dead are not restored without a revert); `dial BotHarrow.DutyPrior 150` puts the guild's harrow back at the Baron's price; revert for the rest.

**26.09.2026 · build 259 (ordered by Patrick ~12:40, written by Opus) · The world is woken round the bots as round a player; nobody goes into a fight it chose without its supplies, and the guild pays; the armour orders that froze thirty thousand gold**
- *Patrick's orders (26.09.2026):* "we wake the world — it must work for them as for players"; "supply and the purchase of every consumable needed — THIS IS COMPULSORY: a mage may not go without reagents for its casts, a healer without bandages, and the other classes have no right to go without bottles and bandages either; set everybody an entry threshold"; and, of the armour orders nobody filled, "sort it out".
- *Decision 1 (the wake):* `bot-proving.json` `Wake: true`, `WakeDeepsOnly: false`: every living bot wakes the 5×5 sectors round it as a client would (`BotWake`, build 251), so creatures walk, look for enemies, cast, breathe and run wherever a bot goes. Shipped together with Decision 2 by Patrick's own sequence: the six awake minutes of 04:08 killed nine unprovisioned bots in the Orc Caves.
- *Decision 2 (the threshold, `BotShops/BotProvision.cs`):* the class's own kit at a share — half its bandages, one of each bottle it carries, half the quiver it was born with, and `Casts` 5 casts of its key spell's reagents (a caster's strongest attack in its book, a healer's greater heal or heal plus cure, anybody else carrying reagents its heal). Every share sits at or below the shopper's own trigger (`BotShopper.Short`, half the kit), so a bot turned away is always a bot the shopper sends for more. Asked at: a delve's leader (`BotDelver.Propose`, `Unsupplied`), the band reckoned for it (`Gather`) and every member called (`BotDelve.Levy`); and a war company going onto somebody else's ground (`BotFeuder.Propose`, after the defence of its own ground, which is answered whatever a bot carries). Not a solo hunt: that is how a poor bot earns its bandages.
- *Decision 3 (supplied, and paid for):* a bot below the threshold buys what it lacks at the spare price (`BotRestock.Spare`, 180/min, counted `Provisioned`) — the shopping price, 12/min, lost to every trade — and what it cannot afford is drawn from its guild's chest (tolls and tithes, `BotChest.Draw`) and then from its guildmates (`BotGuilds.Stand`), into its bank (`BotProvision.Fund`).
- *Decision 4 (the armour orders), from the investigation of 26.09.2026:*
  - *Root cause:* Faron, the one bot on the shard able to sew leather armour, wore out his sewing kit at 01:48:58 and did not replace it for seven and a half hours — a trade tool gone altogether was priced at the shopping price, 12/min, while one merely worn was priced at 180/min. The first kit he bought (09:22:27, 3gp) filled 18 orders for 19,736gp in ten minutes. Meanwhile the armourer's demand counted his skill as if he held the kit, so the orders kept coming, and each new order opened at the highest escalated offer standing, so the anchors ratcheted: Leather Bustier Arms 48 → 862 → 1505gp; raw ribs 37gp apiece; 30,656gp in escrow at 08:42.
  - `BotShopper.Wanting`: a class's own trade tool that is gone altogether is bought at the spare price, as a worn one is.
  - `BotHarness.Ablest`: a tailor counts only with a sewing kit in hand, and at its skill less `BotCraftwork.Margin` — the margin the crafter itself takes orders at.
  - `BotAuction.Worth`: an offer standing on the board is read back no higher than `MostMultiple` × the caller's own estimate, so a fresh want no longer opens at the last one's escalation.
- *Watch:* deaths in the first windows with the world awake; `Unsupplied`, `Provisioned` and the guild's funding line (`BotProvision.Describe`, in the delve summary); whether the shelves run dry of bandages and reagents; the escrow line of the market.
- *Undo:* `dial BotWake.Running false` (or `Wake: false` in the file); `dial BotProvision.Running false`; revert for the rest.

**26.09.2026 · build 258, part 2 (ordered by Patrick ~12:40, written by Opus) · The yard is the hall's square; ground lives only while it reaches the hall; losing the hall's square razes the hall; a new plot must be walkable; a war company musters at its hall**
- *Seen (10:06–12:45):* seven wars between The Lantern and The Blade in two and a half hours. The loser was carried out of "the winner's yard" (a 40-tile radius) towards the winner, into the winner's rings of claims, and into the next war; the last move put its hall at 1082,1402, 1437 steps from home by road for 358 straight, where its own company — still mustering at the old hall — could not reach it, and the seventh war stood still at 22:7 with 27 of 48 bots held in rallies.
- *Patrick's orders (26.09.2026):* "the yard is only the square with the guild's hall; everything else is the zone of influence. If the square with the hall is lost, the hall is razed and may be moved to another square. Squares live while from the square one can reach the square of the guild's hall; if the link is broken, the claim on those lands falls off — three lands in a row, take the land between 1 and 3, then 3 and 2 break: 2 goes to the other guild, 3 breaks because it no longer reaches the guild's lands. When moving — yes, check. Yes, the company may muster at the hall."
- *Decision:*
  - `BotClaim.Seat`: the square a hall stands in is registered as its guild's own, bought, when the hall is raised or adopted (`BotEstate.Register`).
  - `BotLand.Holder`: the yard is the hall's square (and an outpost's square), no longer every tile within 40 of a hall; everything else is the claims'.
  - `BotClaim.Connect` (each `BotClaim.Look`, and at once after a square changes hands): a breadth-first walk from each guild's hall square over its own squares, touching at a side or a corner; every square not reached is dropped and logged. A guild with no hall holds nothing. Not run until the halls are adopted at a boot (`BotEstate.HallsAdopted`).
  - `BotClaim.Settle` → `Lost`: when a square that held the loser's hall changes hands (taken or struck off), `BotEstate.RazeHall` takes the hall and its merchant off the island; the steward raises a new one from the seat, as for any guild without a hall.
  - `BotHolder.Want`: past the hall's own square, only ground touching the guild's own is claimed (a claim that could not connect would fall the moment it was won).
  - `BotPlot.Find` (halls, enlargements, outposts, houses): passes over ground another guild holds, and ground with no road from home or further round by road than `MostBehind` (60) past the search's origin — the far side of a river.
  - `BotFeud`: a war company musters at its guild's hall, read afresh each time, so a hall that moves takes its muster with it.
  - `BotHall`: a hall raised moves the guild's seat to it.
  - `BotExile.AfterWar` off: a lost war no longer sends the loser's hall out of a yard it was never in; hall moves are the square's business now. Verdicts counted as `Superseded`.
- *Expect at the first boot:* squares that do not reach their guild's hall square fall at once (The Lantern's round its old hall at 1178,1500; any held by guilds with no hall).
- *Undo:* revert; `dial BotExile.AfterWar true` restores the exile after a war.

**26.09.2026 · build 258, part 1 (ordered by Patrick ~12:40, written by Opus) · The championship once an hour; the prize drawn on a Fibonacci scale**
- *Seen:* seven championships between 03:19 and 07:42, the marshal (Hermes) calling one whenever the ring stood empty — the last two sixteen minutes apart — and every champion taking a top item: bows and a kryss of vanquishing, an invulnerable ringmail chest, the robe of the arcane mind.
- *Patrick's orders (26.09.2026):* "the tournament once an hour"; "giving a top item every time is really generous — a Fibonacci principle, where 1 is the top item and 55 is just gold".
- *Decision (schedule):* `BotTourney.EveryMs` a week → an hour (the calendar); `LeastGapMs` an hour between one ending and the next being called by anybody but the keyboard (`Start` refuses "too soon", counted `TooSoon`); the marshal offers the tourney only when `BotTourney.Ready`.
- *Decision (prize):* a draw first, weights 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, 21, 34, 55 (out of 142): the top rung (vanquishing / invulnerability, the robe, the steed), then power/fortification, force/hardening, might/guarding, ruin/defense, a pack of supplies (40 bandages, 3 heal and 2 cure potions, 20 of each reagent for a caster, 150 shots for a bow), and purses of 1000, 500 and 250gp. Within an item rung the champion still chooses what it lacks, in the old order; a better prize of the same weapon or piece replaces a worse one (never two), and a champion holding everything at that rung is paid `RepeatPurse`. `IsPrize` now means any magic level. The door's tourney line counts the draws.
